faq_items.question: Can Zoho Books handle manufacturing and bill of materials the way Odoo does?
faq_items.answer: No. Zoho Books tracks stock and composite items but has no bill of materials, work in progress or production costing, so a manufacturer needs Zoho Inventory plus workarounds. Odoo runs manufacturing orders, BOMs, routings and WIP in the same database as the accounts. For a Manesar or Vatva plant that single difference usually settles the choice.

title: How to Set Up GST in Odoo Accounting
content:
To use GST in Odoo you install the Indian Accounting localisation package (l10n_in), set your company state and GSTIN, then let fiscal positions decide whether an invoice carries IGST or CGST plus SGST. Odoo does support Indian GST, and it is compliant when the localisation is set up in the right order: taxes and tax groups first, then fiscal positions, then HSN codes on products, and finally e-invoicing if your turnover requires it. This guide explains each step in plain terms, gives one worked tax calculation, and points you to the parent Odoo Accounting Services page if you would rather have the setup done for you.

Does Odoo support Indian GST?

Yes. Odoo ships a set of India-specific modules that sit on top of its core double-entry engine. The base module, l10n_in, loads the Indian chart of accounts, the standard GST tax codes and the HSN or SAC fields. Companion modules add the Indian GST reports, e-invoicing (IRN) and e-way bill generation. Without these installed, Odoo behaves like a generic international ledger with no concept of CGST, SGST or IGST, so the first real task is always installation.

A short reminder on scope: this article is a setup tutorial. If you are still deciding whether the software fits your business, read our companion piece on whether Odoo is good accounting software for Indian businesses and the honest list of disadvantages of Odoo accounting before you commit.

Which Odoo module do you install for GST?

The mandatory package is l10n_in (Indian Accounting). Install it from the Apps menu before you post any transactions, because it rewrites the chart of accounts and adds the GST tax codes. The related modules you will usually want are the Indian GST reports module, the e-invoicing module and the e-way bill module. Install only what your turnover and business actually need; every extra module is one more thing to keep updated.

Common mistake: Installing the Indian localisation after invoices are already posted. Odoo will not retag historical entries for you, so you are left correcting tax lines and the chart of accounts by hand. Install l10n_in on the very first day the company record is created.

How do you configure GST in Odoo, step by step?

The setup follows a fixed order. Each step depends on the one before it, so resist the urge to jump ahead to raising invoices.

  1. Install l10n_in. Apps, search Indian Accounting, install. This is the foundation and cannot be skipped.
  2. Set the company state and GSTIN. On the company record enter the registered state and the 15-digit GSTIN. The state field is what Odoo reads to decide intra-state versus inter-state tax, so it must be exact.
  3. Check taxes and tax groups. The localisation pre-loads GST 5%, 12%, 18% and 28% as sale and purchase taxes, each split into the correct tax group. Confirm the rates and the linked ledger accounts rather than creating your own from scratch.
  4. Review fiscal positions. Odoo creates intra-state and inter-state fiscal positions that map a single tax to its CGST plus SGST or IGST equivalent. This mapping is the heart of GST in Odoo.
  5. Set HSN or SAC on every product. Enter the code on the product form so the GSTR-1 HSN summary populates itself.
  6. Configure e-invoicing and e-way bills, if applicable. Add the GST Suvidha Provider API credentials generated on the portal so IRNs and e-way bills push automatically.
CA Tip: Set the state on every customer and vendor contact at the point of creation, not later. A blank state is the single most common reason Odoo applies the wrong GST head on an invoice.

How do you create GST tax and tax groups in Odoo?

In most cases you do not create GST taxes at all, because l10n_in supplies them. Each rate exists once as a sale tax and once as a purchase tax, and each belongs to a tax group such as GST 18%. The tax group is what lets a single fiscal position swap an 18% IGST line for a 9% CGST plus 9% SGST pair without you touching the invoice. If you genuinely need a non-standard rate, duplicate an existing GST tax so it inherits the correct tax group and ledger mapping, then edit the percentage. Building a tax from a blank form usually breaks the fiscal position link and the GST reports that depend on it.

How does Odoo decide between IGST and CGST plus SGST?

Odoo compares two states: the state on your company record and the state on the customer's delivery address. When the states match, the intra-state fiscal position applies and the invoice carries CGST and SGST at half the rate each. When they differ, the inter-state fiscal position applies and the invoice carries IGST at the full rate. This logic is automatic, but it is only as reliable as the state data on your contacts.

Worked example: intra-state versus inter-state on a Rs 1,00,000 invoice

Assume a taxable value of Rs 1,00,000 on goods taxed at 18% GST. The table shows how the same invoice splits depending on whether the customer is in the same state as your company or in a different one. Figures are indicative and Exl GST is not relevant here as the tax is the point of the example.

LineIntra-state (same state)Inter-state (different state)
Taxable valueRs 1,00,000Rs 1,00,000
CGST 9%Rs 9,000Rs 0
SGST 9%Rs 9,000Rs 0
IGST 18%Rs 0Rs 18,000
Total taxRs 18,000Rs 18,000
Invoice totalRs 1,18,000Rs 1,18,000

The total tax and the invoice total are identical at Rs 18,000 and Rs 1,18,000; only the split between heads changes. That split is exactly what the fiscal position controls, and getting it wrong means your GSTR-1 reports the tax under the wrong head even though the customer paid the right amount.

Where do HSN codes go, and how much detail is required?

HSN for goods or SAC for services is entered on each product, under the Accounting or Purchase tab, in the HSN or SAC code field added by the localisation. Setting it at product level lets the GSTR-1 HSN summary build automatically instead of being typed in later. On the reporting depth: six-digit HSN is required where aggregate turnover exceeded Rs 5 crore in the previous financial year, and four digits is accepted below that. The current rules and thresholds are published by the CBIC, and it is worth confirming them each year rather than assuming last year's limit still holds.

How do you generate GST invoices and e-invoice IRNs from Odoo?

Once taxes, fiscal positions and HSN codes are in place, a normal customer invoice already carries the correct GST. For e-invoicing, the Indian e-invoicing module connects to a GST Suvidha Provider using API credentials you create on the GST portal. On confirmation Odoo pushes the invoice, receives the IRN and acknowledgement number, and stores the signed QR code on the record. E-invoicing is mandatory for businesses whose aggregate turnover crossed Rs 5 crore in any year from 2017-18 onward, so many growing SMEs now fall inside it. If you also move goods, the e-way bill module generates the bill from the same invoice.

How do you file GST returns from Odoo?

Odoo does not file on your behalf; it prepares the data. Run the GST report under Accounting reporting for the return period, then either export the summary for manual entry or use the GSTR-1 export that produces a JSON file for the GST portal offline utility. Before you upload anything, reconcile the export against the sales register and the credit note register, because amendments and cancelled invoices are the usual source of mismatch. For input tax credit, cross-check the purchase side against your GSTR-2B so you only claim what the portal reflects. The return due dates themselves are governed by the GST law and published on the GST portal, not by the software.

Common mistake: Treating the Odoo GSTR-1 export as final without reconciling cancelled and amended invoices. A single voided invoice that is still counted inflates your outward supply and creates a mismatch the portal will flag at filing.

Is Odoo GST compliant, and how does it compare with the alternatives?

Odoo is GST compliant in India when the localisation is installed and configured correctly; compliance is a function of setup, not of the label. If you are weighing it against other software, our comparison of Odoo versus Zoho Books for an Indian SME goes deeper, and you can read about the equivalent setup on Zoho Books Accounting, Xero Accounting Services or Tally Prime Accounting Services if you have not settled on a platform. The practical difference is that Odoo asks for more configuration up front in exchange for a single system that also runs inventory, sales and manufacturing.

Key terms

  • Odoo Fiscal Positions: the mapping rule that swaps one GST tax for its CGST plus SGST or IGST equivalent based on state.
  • Odoo Double-Entry Engine: the underlying ledger that posts every GST invoice to the correct debit and credit accounts.
  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: reconciling your purchase records against the portal's auto-drafted statement before claiming credit.
  • General Ledger: the master record of all accounts the localisation loads for India.

Key takeaways

  • Install l10n_in before the first invoice; retagging history later is painful.
  • The company state and the customer's delivery state decide IGST versus CGST plus SGST.
  • Fiscal positions do the tax split automatically, so never build GST taxes from a blank form.
  • Put HSN or SAC on every product to auto-build the GSTR-1 HSN summary.
  • Reconcile the Odoo export to your sales and credit note registers before filing.

Set up in the right order, GST in Odoo is dependable and largely hands-off at invoice time. If the configuration or a migration feels heavy, the Odoo Accounting Services team can set the localisation, taxes and fiscal positions for you and hand back a system that files clean.

Decision guide
key_points:
• GST works in Odoo only after the Indian localisation package (l10n_in) is installed, ideally before the first invoice is posted.
  • Odoo chooses between IGST and CGST plus SGST by comparing the company state with the customer's delivery state, driven by fiscal positions.
  • HSN or SAC codes belong on each product so the GSTR-1 HSN summary builds automatically.
  • E-invoicing and e-way bills push from Odoo through a GST Suvidha Provider using portal API credentials.
  • GSTR-1 data leaves Odoo as a summary or a JSON file, but must be reconciled to the sales and credit note registers first.

title: Disadvantages of Odoo Accounting You Should Know
content:
The main disadvantages of Odoo accounting for an Indian business are cost and complexity that do not show up in the sticker price: the software is free to download but usually needs a paid implementation partner, Indian GST and TDS formats are not ready made the way they are in Tally or Zoho Books, customisations break at each yearly version upgrade, and the cloud editions stop working when the internet does. None of this makes Odoo a bad product. It is a full ERP, and used for what it is built for it is powerful. The trouble starts when a small services firm buys it purely as accounting software and discovers the running cost only after go live. This is a critical, honest review of where Odoo accounting falls short for Indian users, and who should look elsewhere. If you want the commercial help side of this, our Odoo Accounting Services page covers implementation and support separately.

What are the disadvantages of Odoo accounting?

Grouped simply, the drawbacks fall into five buckets that most Indian teams meet in this order.

  • Hidden running cost: the free Community edition needs a partner to configure, and Enterprise adds a per user licence on top.
  • Weak out-of-the-box Indian localisation: GST returns, TDS, e-invoicing and e-way bills often need extra modules or developer work.
  • Maintenance and developer dependency: Python modules and XML views give flexibility but mean changes need technical skill.
  • Upgrade churn: a new major version every year, with customisations re-tested each time.
  • Cloud-only editions: no offline working unless you self host.

These are the same categories of limitation you weigh for any package, so read this alongside Is Odoo Good Accounting Software? Pros and Cons for Indian Businesses, which sets out where Odoo genuinely wins before you decide.

Is Odoo 100% free? The cost that appears after go live

No, Odoo is not 100% free in any practical sense for a business. The confusion comes from two things being true at once. Odoo Community is genuinely open source and free to download, and Odoo Enterprise gives one app free for unlimited users on the Odoo Online plan. But accounting on the free Community edition still needs to be installed, configured and connected to your chart of accounts, and the moment you add a second app the free tier ends and the per user Enterprise licence applies to everyone.

The larger cost is people, not licences. Setting up a working Odoo double-entry engine with the correct Odoo fiscal positions for interstate and intrastate GST is partner work. For a small firm the implementation fee, custom Indian modules and a support retainer routinely run to several lakh rupees in year one, which the worked example below sets out in full.

CA Tip: Before signing, ask the partner for a written year-one and year-three total cost of ownership, licence plus implementation plus customisation plus annual support. The three-year figure is where Odoo's real cost against Zoho Books or Tally becomes clear.

Odoo accounting limitations Indian users hit first

The problems Indian teams notice earliest are localisation gaps. Tally and Zoho Books ship Indian statutory formats ready made, so a GSTR-1 or a TDS certificate comes out of the box. Odoo's Indian localisation module exists and has improved, but bespoke needs still surface quickly: a GST report laid out the way your consultant wants it, a TDS section field that is not there by default, an e-invoice IRN flow tuned to your invoicing, or reconciling purchases against GSTR-2B input tax credit matching. Each of these is a change to a Python module or an XML view, which means a developer or partner, not a settings toggle.

TDS is a common early snag. Applying Section 194Q TDS on goods at 0.1% on purchases above the fifty lakh threshold, or lining it up against the seller's TCS, is the kind of India-specific logic that ready-made packages handle in a dropdown and Odoo often handles through configuration or code. For the statutory detail itself, the Income Tax Department and the CBIC GST portal remain the authorities to confirm rates and thresholds against.

Common mistake: Assuming the Indian localisation module makes Odoo compliant on day one. It gives a foundation, not a finished GST and TDS setup. Budget for configuration and testing of returns before you rely on the output for filing.

The maintenance burden and developer dependency

Odoo's greatest strength, that almost anything can be customised, is also its heaviest running cost. Because customisation lives in Python and XML, the useful things a growing business asks for (an approval workflow, a custom cost centre report, a tweaked invoice layout) all need technical hands. Smaller businesses feel this as a standing dependency: a developer or implementation partner effectively on call. A firm that has run Tally on a desktop for years, editing nothing, gets a shock at how much Odoo expects to be actively maintained.

The upgrade cycle sharpens this. Odoo issues a major version each year and supports roughly the three most recent. Custom modules do not carry forward on their own, so custom GST or TDS code has to be re-tested and often rewritten at every upgrade, with the database migrated separately. Fall two or three versions behind and you lose security patches and localisation updates; keep current and you pay for a migration project roughly every year. Our note on how to set up GST in Odoo accounting shows how much of that setup is custom and therefore exposed to this churn.

How safe is Odoo, and does it satisfy Indian audit rules?

On raw security Odoo is sound: it is mature software, Odoo.sh and Odoo Online are professionally hosted, and a self-hosted install is only as safe as your own server management. The sharper question for an Indian company is the audit trail. Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules 2014 requires accounting software to keep an edit log that records every change and cannot be switched off, and the auditor must report on it under Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules 2014.

Odoo logs create and write timestamps on records, but the Community edition trail is thinner than auditors expect, and the fuller audit log features sit in Enterprise. So the honest position is that Odoo can meet the requirement, but often only on Enterprise and after configuration, not automatically on the free edition. Confirm the current rule text on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs site and have your auditor sign off on the setup before your first year end.

Cloud only, and what breaks Odoo when connectivity drops

Odoo Online and Odoo.sh are cloud only. When the internet is down, invoicing, approvals and posting stop; only a self-hosted on-premise install keeps running on a local network. That is a real operational risk at a factory or godown where an invoice and an e-way bill must be raised before a vehicle leaves the gate. Tally, running locally on the machine, keeps working through an outage. This is the practical answer to what breaks Odoo: not the software failing, but the connectivity model not matching a shop-floor reality. If you need offline resilience, either self host, which adds server administration to your maintenance burden, or keep a locally installed package for that site.

What is better than Odoo? Zoho, Xero and Tally compared

There is no single winner. The right tool depends on whether you are buying accounting software or an ERP. For most Indian SMEs that only need books, GST and TDS, a focused package is cheaper and faster. Odoo earns its cost where accounting must sit in one database alongside manufacturing, inventory, CRM and a website. The comparison below is a summary, not a scorecard; weigh it against your own user count and process complexity.

FactorOdooZoho BooksXeroTally Prime
Best suited toFull ERP across departmentsSME accounting and GSTGlobal cloud accountingOffline India-first accounting
Indian GST and TDS out of the boxPartial, needs configurationStrong, ready madeLimited India focusStrong, ready made
Works offlineOnly if self hostedNo, cloud onlyNo, cloud onlyYes, local install
Developer or partner neededUsually yesRarelyRarelyRarely
Yearly upgrade re-testingYes, for customisationsAutomatic, no user effortAutomatic, no user effortMinimal

For deeper side-by-side detail, see Odoo vs Zoho Books: Which Suits an Indian SME?, and compare the service pages for Zoho Books Accounting, Xero Accounting Services and Tally Prime Accounting Services if you are moving off Odoo. Is Odoo better than Xero, or is Zoho better than Odoo? For a services firm that wants zero maintenance, Zoho Books or Xero usually wins; for a manufacturer that wants one system end to end, Odoo can justify itself.

Worked example: the true year-one cost of Odoo for a ten-user SME

Consider a Pune trading firm with ten users moving to Odoo Enterprise for accounting, purchase and inventory. The licence looks modest, but the added heads are where the cost sits. All figures are indicative and Exl GST; your partner's quote will differ.

Cost headBasisYear 1 (indicative, Exl GST)
Enterprise licence10 users x approx. Rs 1,400/user/month x 12Rs 1,68,000
Implementation partnerOne-time setup, chart of accounts, trainingRs 2,00,000
Indian localisation customisationGST report layouts, TDS fields, e-invoice flowRs 80,000
Annual support and AMCRetainer for fixes and small changesRs 40,000
Total year 1Rs 4,88,000

By contrast, a ready-made package covering the same GST and TDS for ten users typically lands in the low tens of thousands per year with no developer. The licence line for Odoo (Rs 1,68,000) is only 34% of the year-one total; the other Rs 3,20,000 is implementation, customisation and support. That gap is the honest cost of Odoo's flexibility, and it is why below about ten users, or for a pure services firm, the numbers rarely favour it. To model the depreciation on any server or hardware you self host, our Depreciation Calculator handles the Schedule II working, and the Ind AS Applicability Checker tells you which reporting framework your entity falls under before you configure the books.

Key terms

  • Odoo Double-Entry Engine: the posting core that turns every Odoo transaction into balanced debits and credits.
  • Odoo Fiscal Positions: Odoo's mechanism for auto-applying the right GST treatment by customer or vendor location.
  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: reconciling purchase records against the auto-drafted GSTR-2B to claim eligible ITC.
  • Section 194Q TDS on Goods: buyer's 0.1% TDS on purchases of goods above the fifty lakh threshold.
  • Double-Entry Bookkeeping: the principle that every entry affects at least two accounts, underpinning any accounting tool.

Key takeaways

  • Odoo is free to download but not free to run; budget for a partner, custom Indian modules and yearly upgrade re-testing.
  • GST, TDS and e-invoicing are not fully ready made the way they are in Tally or Zoho Books.
  • The audit-trail requirement under Rule 3(1) is met more reliably on Enterprise and after configuration; confirm with your auditor.
  • Cloud editions do not work offline, which matters for factories and godowns raising e-way bills.
  • Odoo suits multi-department ERP users with ten-plus users and technical support; smaller and services-only firms usually pay less elsewhere.

Decision guide
key_points:
• Odoo Community is free to download but rarely free to run: an Indian business almost always pays for an implementation partner, custom GST and TDS modules, and yearly upgrade re-testing.
  • Indian statutory formats are not ready made the way they are in Tally or Zoho Books, so GST report layouts, TDS fields and e-invoicing often need a developer.
  • Odoo ships a major version every year and supports roughly the three newest, so customisations must be re-tested and often rewritten at each upgrade.
  • Odoo Online and Odoo.sh are cloud only; invoicing and e-way bills stop when the internet does, unlike a locally installed option.
  • Below about ten users the implementation and partner cost usually outweighs any licence saving.

Below about ten users the implementation and partner cost outweighs any licence saving, and the same GST and TDS compliance runs on Tally or Zoho Books with no developer involved. Odoo earns its cost where accounting must sit in one database with manufacturing, inventory, CRM and a website. A small services firm gets far more system than it needs.

faq_items.question: Can Odoo be used when the internet connection is down?
faq_items.answer: No. Odoo Online and Odoo.sh are cloud only, so invoicing, approvals and posting stop when connectivity stops; only a self hosted on premise install keeps running on a local network. That matters at a factory or godown where an invoice and e-way bill must be raised before a vehicle leaves, which Tally handles locally on the machine.

title: Tally Prime vs Tally ERP 9: What Actually Changed?
content:
The short answer to Tally Prime vs ERP 9 is this: TallyPrime is the current generation of Tally, released in November 2020 to replace Tally.ERP 9. The underlying accounting engine is the same, so your existing books move across intact, but the interface has been rebuilt around a Go To search bar, multitasking across reports and simpler GST and e-invoice workflows. Tally.ERP 9 is no longer sold, its final release was 6.6.3, and statutory updates for it have stopped. This article explains what actually changed, whether the switch is worth doing now, and how the one-way migration works, so you can decide before your next close.

Difference between Tally Prime and ERP 9: what actually changed

Most of what people notice is the interface. Tally.ERP 9 was menu driven: you moved down nested lists to reach a report or voucher. TallyPrime keeps the same double-entry logic underneath but adds a Go To bar that jumps straight to any report, master or voucher by name, and it lets you keep several reports open at once. The masters, groups and ledgers you built over years are untouched, so a bookkeeper who knows ERP 9 is productive in TallyPrime within a day or two.

The bigger, quieter change is compliance. Tally.ERP 9 handles one GSTIN per company and has no built-in e-invoice connectivity. From release 3.0, TallyPrime manages multiple GSTINs in a single company, and it does GSTR-2B reconciliation inside the product (built in since release 2.1), which matters for input tax credit matching. Because ERP 9 no longer receives statutory updates, running it today means the software cannot keep pace with GST portal changes, and that gap only widens each quarter.

AreaTally.ERP 9 (final release 6.6.3)TallyPrime (release 3.0 and later)
Released2009, no longer soldNovember 2020, current product
NavigationMenu driven, nested listsGo To search, multitasking across reports
GSTIN per companyOneMultiple (from 3.0)
GSTR-2B reconciliationNot built inInside the product
E-invoice / e-way billAdd-on or manualConnected workflow
Statutory updatesStoppedOngoing under active TSS
Data compatibilityCannot open Prime dataReads and converts ERP 9 data

Are Tally 9 and ERP 9 the same?

Not quite. Tally 9 was an earlier release from around 2006; Tally.ERP 9 arrived in 2009 and added remote access, payroll and, later, GST. In everyday conversation people say "Tally 9" when they mean Tally.ERP 9, but if you are on a genuinely old Tally 9 build you have two generations to cross, not one. Either way the destination today is TallyPrime, because both older lines are out of active support. If you rely on features like remote Tally access, note that these are carried forward and improved in TallyPrime rather than lost.

Is Tally ERP 9 discontinued?

Tally.ERP 9 is not sold to new users and receives no further product or statutory updates; 6.6.3 was the last release. Existing perpetual licences keep working, so the software will still open and record vouchers. The practical problem is not that it stops running, but that it stops staying compliant: new GST return formats, e-invoice thresholds and portal changes are not delivered to it. For a business that files GST, that is the point at which continuing on ERP 9 becomes a liability rather than a saving. The current e-invoicing threshold applies to businesses with aggregate turnover above five crore rupees, and the mandate is administered through the official GST portal and notified by CBIC.

CA Tip: Before you decide anything, check whether your Tally Software Services (TSS) subscription is still active. The ERP 9 to TallyPrime upgrade is free under active TSS, so a lapsed subscription is usually the only real cost between you and a compliant version.

Can I convert Tally ERP 9 to Tally Prime?

Yes, and the process is built in. When you open an existing Tally.ERP 9 company in TallyPrime, the software offers to migrate it, takes a backup of the old data folder first, then converts the company into the newer structure. You do not re-enter anything. The steps below show the safe sequence; our companion guide on Tally data backup and security best practices covers the backup step in detail.

  1. Take a full, verified backup of every Tally.ERP 9 company, and copy it off the machine.
  2. Install TallyPrime alongside ERP 9; you do not have to uninstall the old version immediately.
  3. Open the company in TallyPrime and accept the migration prompt; it backs up the old folder automatically before converting.
  4. Reconcile the converted company against your last ERP 9 trial balance and key general ledger balances.
  5. Retire ERP 9 only once the numbers tie out and a full period has been closed cleanly in TallyPrime.
Common mistake: Migrating the live company folder without a separate off-machine backup. The conversion is one-way, and if a power cut or disk error interrupts it, the only route back is the pre-migration backup you should already be holding.

Is it possible to open Tally Prime data in Tally ERP 9?

No. Data cannot be opened downwards. TallyPrime rewrites the company into a newer data structure that Tally.ERP 9 simply cannot read, which is exactly why the migration tool backs up the old folder before converting. The only clean way back to ERP 9 is restoring that pre-migration backup. You can export vouchers as XML into a fresh ERP 9 company to recover transactions, but master settings and some configurations will not all survive the round trip. If you work across systems, understanding Tally XML export is worth the time, though for most businesses the honest answer is to commit to TallyPrime rather than plan a retreat.

Which is better, Tally ERP 9 or Tally Prime?

For any business filing GST in India today, TallyPrime is the better choice, because it is the only one of the two still receiving statutory updates. The comparison is less about features and more about compliance risk. ERP 9 will keep recording your double-entry bookkeeping accurately, but it cannot follow the GST portal forward. That said, if you run a niche add-on or a heavily customised TDL setup, test it in TallyPrime before you commit, because some older customisations need a developer to re-point them. Our guides on filing GST returns using TallyPrime and generating e-way bills and e-invoices in Tally show what the newer workflows actually look like, and the common Tally shortcuts and data entry tips ease the transition for your team.

What are the disadvantages of Tally Prime?

TallyPrime is not perfect, and it is fair to name the trade-offs. The recurring complaints are the licence cost with mandatory TSS renewal for statutory updates, slower multi-user performance over a LAN once data grows large, limited native cloud access, and reporting that often has to be exported to Excel for anything beyond the standard formats. Customisation still needs a TDL developer, and heavy manufacturing routing or multi-entity consolidation usually needs a second system. These are the reasons some businesses evaluate cloud alternatives such as Zoho Books accounting, Xero accounting services or Odoo accounting services at the same time as an upgrade, rather than treating the version choice in isolation. If a cloud move is on the table, our note on migration from Tally to Zoho compares the routes.

None of this changes the core recommendation. If you are already committed to Tally, TallyPrime is the version to be on. If you are open to rethinking the platform, weigh it against cloud options while your data is being touched anyway.

Which version of Tally is best: a worked cost example

Because the upgrade is free under active TSS, the real question is the three-year cost of ownership, not the upgrade fee. The table below models a single-user (Silver) licence already owned, comparing an active-TSS path against letting TSS lapse and later paying reactivation plus the compliance risk. All figures are indicative and Exl GST; check current pricing before you budget.

Item (Silver, single user)Stay current: renew TSS yearlyLet TSS lapse, reactivate in year 3
Upgrade ERP 9 to TallyPrimeFree (active TSS)Free once TSS active
TSS year 1 (indicative)4,5000
TSS year 2 (indicative)4,5000
TSS year 3 (indicative)4,5004,500 renewal + 4,500 lapse reactivation
Three-year software spend13,5009,000
Statutory updates receivedAll three yearsNone until year 3
E-invoice / GST compliance gapNilTwo years exposed

The lapse path looks 4,500 rupees cheaper on paper, but it buys two years with no statutory updates, during which a single missed e-invoice mandate or GST format change can cost far more than the saving in penalties and rework. For most filing businesses the current path is the cheaper one once risk is priced in.

Key terms

  • Tally Vault: the built-in password feature that encrypts a Tally company so data cannot be opened without the vault password.
  • Tally XML Export: exporting vouchers and masters as XML, the practical route for moving transactions between Tally companies or versions.
  • Remote Tally Access: connecting to a Tally company from another location, carried forward and improved in TallyPrime.
  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: reconciling purchase records against the auto-drafted GSTR-2B to claim only eligible input tax credit, now handled inside TallyPrime.

Is Tally Prime an ERP?

In the strict sense, TallyPrime is business management and accounting software with strong inventory and statutory features, rather than a full enterprise resource planning suite with manufacturing routing, HR and CRM built in. The "ERP" in Tally.ERP 9 was always a name more than a category. For a small or mid-sized Indian business, TallyPrime does the accounting, GST, inventory and payroll work that matters day to day; if you need deep manufacturing or multi-entity consolidation, that is where a broader ERP or a second system comes in. Once your books are clean and current, keeping compliance on track is far more about process than product, which is where structured Tally Prime accounting services or broader accounting services earn their keep.

Key takeaways

  • TallyPrime replaced Tally.ERP 9 in November 2020; ERP 9 is no longer sold and its last release was 6.6.3.
  • The accounting engine is unchanged, so books migrate intact; the interface, GST and e-invoice workflows are what improved.
  • Migration is one-way: always hold a verified off-machine backup before converting, because ERP 9 cannot open Prime data.
  • The upgrade is free under active TSS; the true cost of staying on ERP 9 is a widening statutory and e-invoice compliance gap.
  • If you are rethinking the platform entirely, weigh TallyPrime against cloud options before you migrate, not after.

Decision guide
key_points:
• TallyPrime, released in November 2020, replaced Tally.ERP 9; Tally.ERP 9 is no longer sold and its final release was 6.6.3.
  • The core accounting engine is the same, so your ledgers, vouchers and reports carry over; what changed is the interface, the Go To search and simplified GST and e-invoice workflows.
  • Migration is one-way: TallyPrime rewrites the data into a newer structure that Tally.ERP 9 cannot open, so a verified backup before you start is not optional.
  • The upgrade itself is free under an active TSS subscription; the real cost of staying on ERP 9 is a growing statutory and e-invoice compliance gap.

title: How to File GST Returns Using Tally Prime
content:
GST in TallyPrime is a built-in feature that tags every sales and purchase voucher with the tax details it needs, so that GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B can be generated straight from your day-to-day entries. You switch it on once in the company settings, record invoices the normal way, clear anything the software cannot classify, and then export a return file to upload on the GST portal. This guide walks through each of those steps, the one figure that tells you a return is ready, and a worked example of the tax computation, written for owners who keep their own books rather than for software trainers.

What GST in TallyPrime means, with a short example

Think of GST in TallyPrime as a layer that sits on top of ordinary double-entry bookkeeping. When you raise a sales invoice for a customer in Maharashtra at 18 per cent, Tally does not just debit the party and credit sales; it also splits the tax into CGST and SGST, records the customer GSTIN, the HSN code and the place of supply, and files that voucher into the correct table of GSTR-1. Sell to a customer in another state and the same voucher is recorded as IGST instead. Because the return is assembled from these tagged vouchers, the quality of your GST filing is only ever as good as the quality of your data entry, which is why the setup and the review stages below matter more than the filing click itself.

How to activate GST in TallyPrime

GST is not on by default in a fresh company. To activate it, open the company, go to Features (F11), and set Enable Goods and Services Tax (GST) to Yes. TallyPrime then asks for the details that drive every later calculation, so enter them carefully:

  1. State and registration type (Regular or Composition), which decides whether you file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B or the composition return.
  2. Your GSTIN, which prints on invoices and appears on the return.
  3. The applicability date, so historical vouchers before GST registration are not pulled into a return.
  4. The default rate and periodicity (monthly or quarterly), which should match the periodicity you chose on the portal.

Get the registration type and the periodicity right at this stage. A regular dealer wrongly set to composition, or a QRMP taxpayer set to monthly, produces returns that will not reconcile with the portal later. If you also handle e-invoicing or e-way bills, those credentials are entered in the same GST details screen; the mechanics of that are covered separately in our note on generating e-way bills and e-invoices in Tally.

CA Tip: Set the applicability date to your actual GST registration date, not the date you started using Tally. This one field stops pre-registration invoices leaking into your first return, a common cause of a GSTR-1 value that does not tie to the books.

Creating GST ledgers and stock items

For the tax to compute, three things need a rate: the sales and purchase ledgers, the stock items or service ledgers, and the tax ledgers themselves. Create separate duty ledgers for CGST, SGST, IGST and Cess under the group Duties & Taxes, each with the tax type set correctly. On each stock item, set the GST rate and HSN or SAC code; where a whole ledger carries one rate you can set it at ledger level instead. TallyPrime supports rate setup at the company, group, ledger and item level, and the most specific level wins, so decide early where your rates will live to avoid two different rates fighting on the same invoice. All of this posts through the general ledger exactly like any other master, so nothing about the underlying accounting changes.

Common mistake: Leaving the HSN code blank on a stock item. The invoice still saves, but the voucher lands in the Uncertain Transactions list and drops out of GSTR-1 until you fix it. Fill HSN and SAC codes at the master stage, not at filing time.

Recording a GST invoice and a GST entry in Tally

Once masters carry rates, a GST entry is an ordinary voucher. Record a sale through Voucher (F8 for sales), select the party, add the stock items, and TallyPrime calculates CGST and SGST or IGST automatically from the place of supply. Select the GST tax ledgers to complete the entry and the invoice is ready to print with the tax breakup, the GSTIN of both parties and the HSN summary. Purchases work the same way through the purchase voucher, and the input tax on them becomes your claimable credit. If you record a lot of vouchers a day, the muscle-memory shortcuts in our guide to common Tally shortcuts and data-entry tips save real time, since GST accuracy depends on consistent entry more than anything else. Every one of these entries is, at heart, a journal entry with a tax tag attached.

How to get GST data ready: the Uncertain Transactions list

This is the step most tutorials skip and the one that decides whether your return is clean. Open the GST report (Gateway of Tally > Display More Reports > GST Reports > GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B). Every voucher for the period is sorted into Included in return, Not relevant or Uncertain Transactions. An uncertain transaction is one TallyPrime cannot place because a detail is missing or contradictory: a blank or invalid party GSTIN, a missing HSN code, a tax rate that does not match the ledger, or a state that conflicts with the place of supply. Drill into the list, fix each voucher, and watch the count fall to zero. A return generated with a non-zero uncertain count silently omits those invoices, so treat that figure, not the deadline, as your green light to file.

GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B in TallyPrime, and how filing actually happens

GSTR-1 is your outward-supply return: the invoice-level list of what you sold. GSTR-3B is the monthly or quarterly summary that nets your output tax against input tax credit and shows the cash payable. In TallyPrime, GSTR-3B is a report that reads your vouchers and lays them out in the exact boxes of the portal form, so you can see the liability before you file. What TallyPrime does not do is file on your behalf: for GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B it exports the data as a JSON file that you upload on the GST portal or through the government offline tool. Newer releases can also connect to the portal to push data directly, but the legal act of filing, with your OTP or DSC, stays on the portal. The CBIC keeps the current return formats and due dates on its GST resources site; check them each year rather than relying on a rate memorised from an old assessment.

Worked example: computing net GST payable in GSTR-3B

Take a Maharashtra trader for one month. All supplies and purchases are at 18 per cent. The table shows how TallyPrime nets output tax against input tax credit to arrive at the cash actually payable. Figures are illustrative.

HeadOutput tax (on sales)Input tax credit (on purchases)Net cash payable
IGST (inter-state, sales 5,00,000; purchases 2,00,000)90,00036,00054,000
CGST (intra-state, sales 10,00,000; purchases 6,00,000)90,00054,00036,000
SGST (intra-state, sales 10,00,000; purchases 6,00,000)90,00054,00036,000
Total2,70,0001,44,0001,26,000

Output tax of 2,70,000 less eligible credit of 1,44,000 leaves 1,26,000 to pay in cash for the month. TallyPrime shows this same summary in the GSTR-3B report, which is why the reconciliation in the next section matters: if the credit figure in your books is higher than what the portal actually allows, your real cash outflow is larger than the report suggests.

Reconciling GSTR-2B before you file

Your input tax credit is only safe to the extent it appears in GSTR-2B, the static statement the portal builds from your suppliers' filings. Download the GSTR-2B JSON for the period from the portal and import it into TallyPrime, then open the reconciliation view. Tally matches supplier GSTIN, invoice number, date and value, and sorts every line into fully matched, partially matched, available only in your books, or available only on the portal. Anything sitting in books only is credit a supplier has not yet reported, and claiming it in GSTR-3B is a risk. Clearing this list before you finalise GSTR-3B is the single biggest protection for your credit claim; the mechanics of the match are explained in our glossary note on GSTR-2B input tax credit matching.

CA Tip: Reconcile GSTR-2B weekly, not on the 19th. Chasing a supplier to file before your GSTR-3B deadline is far easier when you have three weeks of notice rather than one day. Keep an encrypted backup of the company using Tally Vault so the reconciled data cannot be tampered with.

If you outgrow Tally, or never started on it

TallyPrime suits businesses that want the ledger on their own machine and a filing workflow they control. If you are weighing it against a cloud stack, the same GST logic carries over to Zoho Books accounting, Xero accounting and Odoo accounting, each with its own reconciliation view. If you are still on the older engine, our comparison of TallyPrime versus Tally ERP 9 covers what changed for GST specifically, and it is worth keeping a disciplined Tally data backup routine whichever version you run, since a corrupt company file the week of filing is a problem no return format can fix. Setting up the GST configuration correctly the first time is exactly where our Tally Prime accounting services team spends its effort, because a clean master saves a dozen uncertain-transaction fixes later.

Key terms

  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: comparing the portal's supplier-reported credit statement against your purchase register before you claim.
  • General Ledger: the master record of every account into which GST vouchers post like any other entry.
  • Journal Entry: the underlying debit-and-credit record that a GST voucher extends with a tax tag.
  • Tally Vault: TallyPrime's password feature that encrypts the company data file.

Key takeaways

  • Activate GST once in Company Features and enter the state, GSTIN, registration type and periodicity accurately; these fields drive every later calculation.
  • Set HSN or SAC codes and rates at the master stage so vouchers do not fall into the Uncertain Transactions list.
  • Drive the Uncertain Transactions count to zero before generating any return; a non-zero count silently drops invoices.
  • TallyPrime prepares and exports the return as JSON, but filing with OTP or DSC happens on the GST portal.
  • Reconcile GSTR-2B before finalising GSTR-3B so your input tax credit is one the portal will actually allow.

Decision guide
key_points:
• GST in TallyPrime is a feature you switch on in Company GST Details, after which every sales and purchase voucher is tagged for the return automatically.
  • The number that decides whether a return is clean is the Uncertain Transactions count: it must be zero before you generate GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B.
  • TallyPrime prepares and exports the return as a JSON file; the actual filing still happens on the GST portal, so treat Tally as the books-of-account source, not the filing counter.
  • Reconcile the portal GSTR-2B against your purchase register inside Tally before you accept input tax credit in GSTR-3B.

faq_items.question: How is GSTR-2B reconciled in TallyPrime?
faq_items.answer: Download the GSTR-2B JSON for the period from the GST portal and import it through the GST reports, then open the reconciliation view. TallyPrime matches supplier GSTIN, invoice number, date and value, and sorts rows into fully matched, partially matched, available only in books and available only on the portal. Clearing that mismatch list before GSTR-3B protects the credit claim.

faq_items.question: How is an e-invoice generated in TallyPrime?
faq_items.answer: Set the e-invoicing applicability date and the invoice registration portal credentials in the company GST details, then record the sales voucher and send it for IRN generation while saving. TallyPrime uploads the details and prints the invoice reference number, acknowledgement number and signed QR code on the invoice. Bulk generation is available for invoices left pending.

faq_items.question: How is an e-invoice cancelled in TallyPrime?
faq_items.answer: An invoice reference number can be cancelled within 24 hours of generation. Open the voucher, choose the e-invoice cancellation option, enter the reason and remarks, and TallyPrime sends the request to the invoice registration portal and marks the voucher accordingly. After 24 hours the IRN cannot be cancelled and the correction has to run through a credit note reported in GSTR-1.

faq_items.question: How is an e-way bill generated in TallyPrime?
faq_items.answer: Enter the e-way bill portal credentials in the company GST details, and while saving a qualifying sales invoice TallyPrime asks for transport details, sends them to the portal and brings back the e-way bill number and validity. Bills can also be generated in bulk or exported as a JSON file for manual upload where connectivity at the despatch point is poor.

faq_items.question: What does an uncertain transaction mean in the TallyPrime GST report?
faq_items.answer: Uncertain transactions are vouchers TallyPrime cannot place in the return because information is missing or contradictory: a blank or invalid party GSTIN, a missing HSN code, a tax rate that does not match the ledger, or a state that conflicts with the place of supply. Clear this list before generating GSTR-1, otherwise those invoices drop out of the return.

title: Common Tally Shortcuts and Data Entry Tips
content:
Common TallyPrime shortcuts and data entry tips come down to a small set of keys that cut entry time (Alt+G to jump anywhere, F4 to F9 for the voucher types, Alt+2 to duplicate, Alt+C to create a master and Ctrl+A to save) plus a handful of habits that stop wrong postings before they reach the trial balance. This guide lists the shortcuts that matter in day-to-day bookkeeping and the checks that keep the data clean, so a team can post more in less time without quietly misstating the accounts. If you want the software set up and run for you rather than learned from scratch, that is a job for our Tally Prime Accounting Services; everything below is for accountants doing the entry themselves.

What are TallyPrime shortcut keys?

TallyPrime shortcut keys are keyboard combinations that open a voucher, a report or a master, or that accept and save the current screen, without reaching for the mouse. TallyPrime redesigned navigation around two of them. Alt+G opens Go To, which jumps straight to any report, voucher or master by typing part of its name from wherever you happen to be. Ctrl+G is Switch To, which changes the active screen instead of stacking a new one on top of it. Between them they replace most of the menu walking that Tally.ERP 9 users were trained on, which is the single biggest change to appreciate if you have moved across (our note on Tally Prime vs Tally ERP 9 covers the rest of what shifted).

The rest of the shortcuts fall into three groups: function keys that pick a voucher type, Alt combinations that act on the whole voucher or report (export, print, duplicate, delete), and Ctrl combinations that either save or open the second voucher in a family. Learn the group logic once and you rarely need a printed cheat sheet again.

TallyPrime function keys F1 to F12

The function keys are the backbone of data entry, and the use of F1 to F12 in Tally is worth committing to memory because they are the same on every accounting voucher screen.

  • F1: Help, and on the Gateway it also handles company selection.
  • F2: change the voucher date. Alt+F2 changes the period (the date range) of a report.
  • F4: Contra. F5: Payment. F6: Receipt. F7: Journal.
  • F8: Sales. F9: Purchase. These are the two you press most, and each has a Ctrl partner for its credit or debit note.
  • F10: other vouchers (memorandum, reversing journal and the like).
  • F11: company Features. F12: Configure, where you switch on options such as separate buyer and consignee details or additional narration lines.

The use of the F8 key in Tally is simply to open a Sales voucher, which is why F8 is usually the busiest key in a trading business.

Shortcut keys for data entry in TallyPrime

These are the shortcut keys for data entry in Tally that earn their keep across a full day of posting. Keep this list beside you for the first week and it will become muscle memory soon after.

TaskShortcutWhere it works
Go To (search anything)Alt+GAnywhere
Switch To (change screen)Ctrl+GAnywhere
Create a master on the flyAlt+CInside a voucher field
Duplicate the current voucherAlt+2Day book / voucher
Accept and save the screenCtrl+AVouchers, masters, config
Cancel a voucherAlt+XVoucher / day book
Delete a voucher or lineAlt+DVoucher / day book
Credit NoteCtrl+F8Voucher entry
Debit NoteCtrl+F9Voucher entry
Export the current report or voucherAlt+EAny report / voucher

Two of these change how a team works. Alt+C creates a master, a new supplier ledger or a stock item, without leaving the entry screen, so entry does not stall while someone sets up the chart of accounts. Alt+2 opens a fresh voucher pre-filled with the same ledgers and amounts as the one you are looking at, which turns a repetitive purchase run into a few keystrokes. Each of these entries still resolves to a journal entry in the background and posts to the general ledger exactly as a manual entry would, so the discipline of correct grouping does not go away just because the entry is faster.

CA Tip: When you create a supplier or ledger with Alt+C, set the correct group in that same moment. A ledger parked under the wrong group (say a supplier placed under indirect expenses) quietly misstates the balance sheet and is painful to unwind after a quarter of postings.

The 18 voucher types in TallyPrime

People ask what the 18 vouchers in Tally are because that is the count of predefined voucher types that ship with the software. They split into accounting, inventory and order categories.

  • Accounting: Contra (F4), Payment (F5), Receipt (F6), Journal (F7), Sales (F8), Credit Note (Ctrl+F8), Purchase (F9) and Debit Note (Ctrl+F9).
  • Order and delivery: Sales Order, Purchase Order, Receipt Note, Delivery Note, Rejections In and Rejections Out.
  • Inventory and control: Stock Journal, Physical Stock, Memorandum and Reversing Journal.

That is eighteen. You can add your own voucher types on top (a separate series for cash sales, for example), but knowing which shortcut opens which predefined type is what makes entry quick. For GST work the Sales, Purchase, Credit Note and Debit Note vouchers feed the returns directly, which we walk through in the guide on filing GST returns using Tally Prime.

Alt+E, Ctrl+F8, Ctrl+F2 and the combinations people ask about

Alt+E in TallyPrime opens the Export screen for whatever report or voucher is on display, so a day book, a ledger or a GSTR summary can be pushed to Excel, PDF or XML in a couple of steps. It pairs with Alt+P (print) and Alt+M (e-mail). If you export ledgers to move data between companies or into another tool, that is the Tally XML export route.

Ctrl+F8 in TallyPrime is used to open a Credit Note, the voucher you raise when a customer returns goods or you issue a sales credit; its mirror, Ctrl+F9, opens the Debit Note for purchase returns.

The Ctrl+F2 shortcut is the one that causes confusion, because the key people actually want is usually Alt+F2. In TallyPrime, F2 changes the working date of the voucher and Alt+F2 changes the period (the date range) of a report, which is what most users mean when they talk about changing the range on screen. If a keystroke does not behave the way an old habit expects, check F2 and Alt+F2 first before assuming the shortcut is broken.

Common mistake: Duplicating a purchase voucher with Alt+2 and saving it without changing the supplier invoice number and date. Duplicating without editing the reference is the commonest cause of duplicate purchase entries, and it inflates both expenses and input tax credit until someone reconciles it away.

A fast, error-light entry workflow

Speed on its own is not the goal; a fast workflow that also lands the entry in the right place is. Here is a sequence that a team can standardise on for repetitive purchase entry.

  1. Press Alt+G and type the voucher you want, or press F9 straight into a Purchase voucher.
  2. At the supplier field, if the ledger does not exist, press Alt+C and create it under the correct group.
  3. Enter the taxable value and let the GST ledgers pick up automatically from the stock item or ledger setup.
  4. Add the supplier invoice number and date in the reference field. Never skip this.
  5. Press Ctrl+A to accept and save without stepping through the remaining fields.
  6. For the next similar invoice, open it from the day book and press Alt+2 to duplicate, then repeat step 4.

Standardising this order matters more than raw typing speed, because it puts the reference edit (step 4) in the path every single time, which is exactly where duplicate and misdated entries creep in.

Data entry tips that prevent errors

The shortcuts save minutes; these habits save reconciliations. A clean set of books is easier to audit and turns into a reliable trial balance at period close, which is the whole point of double-entry bookkeeping in the first place.

Enforce narration and references

A blank narration or a missing invoice number is invisible on the day of entry and expensive at year end. Use F12 configuration to make narration compulsory on the vouchers that need it, and treat the supplier reference as mandatory on every purchase.

Run exception reports before you close

At month end, run the exception reports before closing: negative stock, negative cash, ledgers with no movement, and vouchers with blank narration. Then scan the day book for entries dated outside the period and for suspiciously round sum amounts. Reconcile the bank while you are there, because a clean bank reconciliation catches entries that never happened and payments posted twice.

Rely on the edit log

The edit log, mandatory for companies from 1 April 2023 under Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, records exactly what was altered after posting and by whom. It is now a statutory feature rather than an optional one, so treat it as your audit trail and do not switch it off; the requirement is set out by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Where GST vouchers feed e-invoicing or e-way bills, the same discipline applies, and the field rules published on the CBIC GST portal are the authority on what each document must carry (our walkthrough on generating e-way bills and e-invoices in Tally shows the entry side).

CA Tip: Restrict Alt+C master creation for junior users once the chart of accounts has settled. On-the-fly ledger creation is a gift on go-live day and a liability a year later, when you find four spellings of the same supplier scattered across the ledgers.

Worked example: recording a GST purchase voucher

Take an intra-state purchase of raw material worth ₹50,000 (indicative, Exl GST) at 18% GST, split as CGST 9% and SGST 9%. You would open the voucher with F9, create the supplier with Alt+C if needed, and save with Ctrl+A. The posting behind those keystrokes looks like this.

LedgerDr / CrAmount (₹)
Purchase (raw material)Dr50,000
Input CGST @ 9%Dr4,500
Input SGST @ 9%Dr4,500
Supplier (sundry creditor)Cr59,000
Total59,000 = 59,000

The debits (50,000 + 4,500 + 4,500 = 59,000) equal the single credit to the supplier, so the voucher balances and the ₹9,000 of input tax sits ready to be matched against the return. If you duplicate this voucher with Alt+2 for the next invoice from the same supplier, change only the invoice number, date and value; the ledger structure carries over correctly.

Key terms

  • Journal Entry: the debit-and-credit record that every Tally voucher resolves to behind the screen.
  • General Ledger: the master record where all voucher postings accumulate by account.
  • Trial Balance: the list of ledger balances that must agree, and where entry errors surface.
  • Tally Vault: the password feature that encrypts a company's data so shortcuts do not become a security gap.

Key takeaways

  • Alt+G (Go To) and Ctrl+G (Switch To) replace most menu navigation in TallyPrime; learn these two first.
  • Voucher types live on F4 to F9, with Ctrl+F8 for Credit Note and Ctrl+F9 for Debit Note.
  • Alt+2 (duplicate) and Alt+C (create master) are the biggest time savers, but only if you edit the reference and set the right group before saving.
  • Ctrl+A saves any screen instantly; use it, but never let a stray Enter commit a half-finished entry.
  • Run exception reports and keep the edit log on: clean data matters as much as fast data.

Once entry is under control in Tally, the same discipline transfers to other stacks if you migrate later, whether that is Zoho Books Accounting, Xero Accounting Services or Odoo Accounting Services; and if fixed assets are part of your postings, the depreciation calculator helps schedule the charge. Protect the data behind all of it by following our note on Tally data backup and security best practices.

Decision guide
key_points:
• TallyPrime replaced most menu navigation with two search shortcuts: Alt+G (Go To) and Ctrl+G (Switch To), which do most of the heavy lifting on a busy entry day.
  • The voucher keys sit on F4 to F9: Contra, Payment, Receipt, Journal, Sales and Purchase, with Ctrl+F8 for Credit Note and Ctrl+F9 for Debit Note.
  • Alt+2 duplicates a voucher and Alt+C creates a master on the fly, the two biggest time savers on repetitive entries, provided you edit the reference before saving.
  • Ctrl+A accepts and saves any screen without stepping through the remaining fields.
  • Speed only helps if the numbers are right, so exception reports and the mandatory edit log matter as much as the keystrokes.

title: How to Generate E-Way Bills and E-Invoices in Tally
content:
An e-invoice in Tally is an ordinary GST sales voucher that TallyPrime transmits to the government Invoice Registration Portal (IRP), which validates it and returns three things the software writes straight back into the voucher: a unique Invoice Reference Number (IRN), a digitally signed QR code, and, where transport details are supplied, the e-way bill number. In other words you do not create a separate document. You record the sale as usual and let Tally exchange the data with the portal, so the printed invoice already carries the IRN, the QR code and, on a moving consignment, the e-way bill, without leaving the voucher screen. This guide explains the rule, the turnover threshold and the practical steps for both e-invoices and e-way bills. If you want a team to run your books and file for you, that sits with our Tally Prime Accounting Services.

What is e-invoicing in Tally?

E-invoicing is the process of reporting a B2B invoice to a government portal at the moment it is raised, rather than filing it later in a return. The portal authenticates the invoice, stamps it with the IRN and QR code, and pushes the same data into your GSTR-1 and the buyer's records. TallyPrime is not the portal; it is the accounting layer that packages the voucher into the required JSON schema, sends it, and stores the response. Because the invoice is validated the moment it is created, the buyer's GSTR-2B input tax credit matching becomes far cleaner, since the same figures appear on both sides from the start.

This is a feature how-to, not a return-filing guide. Once your invoices carry IRNs, the monthly GSTR-1 largely auto-populates, and we cover that separately in how to file GST returns using Tally Prime.

Who is eligible for e-invoicing? The turnover limit

E-invoicing is mandatory for a GST registered business whose aggregate turnover crossed Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onward. Once you cross the line in any year, the obligation stays with you even if turnover later falls below Rs 5 crore. So the common question, "is e-invoicing mandatory for 5 crore turnover?", has a plain answer: yes, at Rs 5 crore aggregate turnover the mandate applies.

It applies to B2B supplies, exports and supplies to SEZ units. B2C invoices stay outside the mandate. A short list of businesses is exempt whatever their turnover: banks and financial institutions, insurers, goods transport agencies, passenger transport operators, cinema multiplex operators and SEZ units. Note that the exemption is on the supplier's status, not the customer's. The threshold and the current list are maintained on the government GST portal and the CBIC site, and it is worth checking them each year because the figure has been lowered in stages.

CA Tip: Aggregate turnover is measured across all GSTINs on the same PAN, on an all-India basis. A business with several branch registrations can cross Rs 5 crore in total while each branch looks small, so check the PAN-level figure, not the state one.

How do I enable e-invoicing in Tally Prime?

Enabling is a one-time setup on the company. The steps are the same on a fresh company or one you have used for years.

  1. Open the company, press F11 for Features, and set Enable Goods and Services Tax (GST) to Yes.
  2. In the GST details screen, set e-Invoicing applicable to Yes, and enter your applicable-from date and the bill-from place.
  3. Set Send e-Way Bill details with e-Invoice to Yes if you want both generated together.
  4. Confirm your GSTIN and the registered e-invoice user credentials, which Tally uses to authenticate with the portal through the connected GST Suvidha Provider (GSP).

That is all the configuration needed. On older TallyPrime releases the labels differ slightly, and the earlier Tally.ERP 9 handled e-invoicing through an add-on rather than natively, which is one of several reasons to move up: we compare the two in Tally Prime vs Tally ERP 9: what actually changed.

E-invoice process in Tally: how to generate one step by step

With the feature enabled, generating an e-invoice is part of recording the sale. There is no separate menu to hunt for.

  1. Record the sales voucher as normal, with the correct GST ledgers, HSN codes and the buyer's GSTIN.
  2. If the goods are moving, add the transporter name, distance in kilometres, mode of transport and vehicle number in the voucher's e-way bill details.
  3. Accept the voucher, then choose Exchange and Send for e-Invoicing (or Send for e-Way Bill).
  4. Tally converts the voucher into the JSON schema and transmits it to the IRP through the GSP. This step is the same Tally XML export mechanism, wrapped for the portal.
  5. The portal validates and returns the IRN, the signed QR code and, where Part B is present, the e-way bill number and validity date.
  6. Tally writes all three back against the voucher, and the printed invoice carries the QR code so it is a valid tax invoice.

To do this the machine needs live connectivity to the portal, whether that is direct or via remote Tally access on a networked server. Keyboard-driven users will find the whole flow quicker with the muscle memory covered in our common Tally shortcuts and data entry tips.

What is an e-way bill, and how does it fit in?

An e-way bill is an electronic document raised before goods worth more than Rs 50,000 move. It carries a 12-digit e-way bill number the transporter must produce on demand. Rule 138 of the CGST Rules makes it compulsory for inter-state movement and for intra-state movement above the state threshold. Part A holds the invoice and party details; Part B holds the vehicle and transport details. Because the e-way bill draws on the very invoice data already sitting in Tally, generating it from the voucher avoids re-keying and the transposition errors that come with it. Where a transporter moves several consignments in one vehicle, each consignment still carries its own e-way bill, and the transporter combines them into a consolidated e-way bill in Form GST EWB-02 on the portal. If the movement is by a goods transport agency under reverse charge, the e-way bill obligation and the RCM tax treatment are separate points to get right.

Common mistake: Treating the consignment value as the taxable value alone. The Rs 50,000 e-way bill limit is tested on the invoice value including GST but excluding any exempt goods, so an order with a taxable value just under Rs 50,000 can still cross the line once tax is added.

Does an e-invoice create the e-way bill automatically?

Yes, where Part B transport details accompany the invoice. In that case the portal returns the IRN, the signed QR code and the e-way bill number in a single call, and TallyPrime stores all three against the voucher. If the vehicle number is not ready when you raise the invoice, the portal issues only the IRN, and Part B is filled in later on the e-way bill portal before movement starts. This split matters for a warehouse that invoices in the morning and despatches in the afternoon: the IRN can go out early, and the e-way bill can be completed once the vehicle is assigned.

What is the 30-day limit for an e-invoice?

The portal will not accept an invoice reported too late. Businesses with an aggregate turnover of Rs 10 crore or more must report each invoice to the IRP within 30 days of the invoice date. Report it on the 31st day and the portal rejects it, leaving you with an invoice that cannot legally carry an IRN. The practical discipline is simple: send invoices for IRN daily, not in a month-end batch. For a business near the threshold this is the single most common cause of blocked invoices, and it is entirely avoidable with a daily Exchange run.

CA Tip: Build a short daily routine: raise sales, run Exchange and Send, then check the exchange summary for any invoice the portal rejected. Fixing a rejection on the same day is trivial; discovering it three weeks later, after the goods have already moved, is not.

How to check e-invoice details in Tally

TallyPrime keeps a running status for every voucher. From the Gateway of Tally, open the GST reports and the e-Invoice report, which lists invoices by status: pending, exported, and accepted with IRN. You can drill into any voucher to see the IRN, the acknowledgement number, the acknowledgement date and the e-way bill number and its validity. A voucher that failed validation shows the portal's error message, so you can correct the GSTIN, HSN or value and resend. Keeping these records safe matters as much as filing them; our note on Tally data backup and security best practices and the built-in Tally Vault password both help here.

One clarification worth making, since it confuses people: e-invoicing is not the same as your withholding obligations. Charges such as Section 194Q TDS on goods and Section 52 TCS under GST apply to different transactions and are recorded separately, whatever the e-invoice status of the underlying bill.

Worked example: an invoice that triggers both an IRN and an e-way bill

Suppose a Maharashtra manufacturer with turnover above Rs 5 crore raises an inter-state B2B sale of machine parts to a buyer in Gujarat and despatches the goods the same day. Because turnover is above the mandate and this is a B2B inter-state supply of moving goods, both an e-invoice and an e-way bill are due. The consignment value for the e-way bill test is the invoice value including GST. The figures below are illustrative.

LineAmount (Rs)
Taxable value of goods1,20,000
IGST at 18%21,600
Total invoice value (consignment value)1,41,600
E-way bill threshold50,000
E-way bill required?Yes (1,41,600 is above 50,000)
E-invoice required?Yes (B2B, turnover above Rs 5 crore)

In Tally the manufacturer records the sale, adds the vehicle number and distance in the e-way bill details, and runs Exchange and Send. The portal returns the IRN, the QR code and the e-way bill number in one call, with the e-way bill validity calculated from the distance. The printed invoice then carries the QR code and the e-way bill number, and the transporter can produce it on demand.

Key terms

  • Tally XML Export: the structured data export Tally wraps into the JSON schema sent to the invoice portal.
  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: reconciling purchase credits against the auto-drafted GSTR-2B, which e-invoicing makes cleaner.
  • Goods Transport Agency (GTA) RCM: reverse-charge GST on freight, a separate point from the e-way bill itself.
  • Tally Vault: the password feature that encrypts company data at rest.

Key takeaways

  • An e-invoice in Tally is a normal sales voucher sent to the portal, which returns the IRN, QR code and, with transport details, the e-way bill number.
  • The mandate applies at Rs 5 crore aggregate turnover in any year from 2017-18, for B2B, export and SEZ supplies.
  • An e-way bill is required above Rs 50,000 consignment value, tested on the invoice value including GST.
  • Enable both under F11, add transport details in the voucher, and use Exchange and Send.
  • Report invoices within 30 days if turnover is Rs 10 crore or more, so send for IRN daily.

The same reporting logic exists in other packages, so if you are weighing up a change, our informational overviews of Zoho Books accounting, Xero accounting services and Odoo accounting services set out how each handles GST and e-invoicing, and the statutory positions above are always worth confirming against the live CBIC GST notifications.

Decision guide
key_points:
• An e-invoice in Tally is a normal GST sales voucher that TallyPrime sends to the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), a signed QR code and (where transport details are added) the e-way bill number, all written back into the same voucher.
  • E-invoicing is mandatory for a GST registered business whose aggregate turnover crossed Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onward, for B2B supplies, exports and supplies to SEZ units.
  • An e-way bill is required before goods worth more than Rs 50,000 move; when Part B transport details are present, the portal issues the IRN and the e-way bill in a single call.
  • Enable both under F11 statutory features, add transporter and vehicle details in the voucher, then use Exchange and Send to push the data through the connected GSP.
  • Businesses with aggregate turnover of Rs 10 crore or more must report invoices to the portal within 30 days of the invoice date.
