title: Tally Data Backup and Security Best Practices
content:
The best practice for Tally data backup is simple to state and easy to neglect: keep at least one dated copy of your company data on a second drive and one in the cloud, close the company before you copy it, and test a restore before you ever need it. A single copy of the numbered company folder on one computer is not a backup. It is one power surge, one ransomware click or one stolen laptop away from a year of lost vouchers. This guide sets out a routine that survives file corruption, not only hardware failure, and shows how to restore and recover data when something does go wrong.

Where is Tally data stored?

TallyPrime keeps each company in a numbered folder (for example 10001, 10002) inside its data directory. By default that path is the Data folder under the Tally installation, but you can see and change it at Gateway of Tally, then F1 (Help), then Settings, then Data Configuration. The folder holds the transaction and master files that make up your accounts, so this numbered folder is exactly what any backup routine has to protect. Knowing the path matters: if you have never checked it, your backups may be pointing at an empty or wrong directory.

Because the data sits as ordinary files on disk, it is exposed to the same risks as any other file: disk failure, accidental deletion, corruption during an improper shutdown, and malware. Understanding your numbered folder is also the first step before you copy data to another computer or migrate it into a cloud system such as Zoho Books Accounting, Xero Accounting Services or Odoo Accounting Services.

How do you back up data in Tally?

TallyPrime has a built-in backup: go to Gateway of Tally, then Data, then Backup, choose the source company and a destination path, and confirm. Tally writes two files, TBK900.001 (the data) and TBK900.CFG (the configuration), into the destination folder. There is no single dedicated keyboard shortcut for backup in TallyPrime; you reach it through the Data menu, so if someone tells you a magic hotkey, treat it with caution. Learning the wider set of movement keys does help you work faster, and our note on common Tally shortcuts and data entry tips covers those.

The built-in backup is useful but limited. It writes to a path you choose, and if that path is another folder on the same disk, a disk failure takes both the original and the backup. Best practice is to point the destination at a different physical drive and then copy that backup off-site or to the cloud on a schedule.

CA Tip: Name each backup folder with the date, such as Tally_Backup_2026-07-24, and never overwrite yesterday's copy. Corruption is often discovered days later, so a single rolling backup can quietly copy the corrupted data over your last good one.

How to set up Tally auto backup

TallyPrime has no built-in scheduler, so automation is done outside the application using Windows Task Scheduler. The reliable pattern is:

  1. Write a short script (a .bat file) that copies the numbered company folder to a second drive and to a synced cloud folder, into a new dated sub-folder each run.
  2. Make sure everyone has closed the company in Tally before the job runs; a file open inside Tally can copy incompletely.
  3. Open Windows Task Scheduler, create a task, and point it at the script.
  4. Set the trigger for after business hours, for example 9:30 pm daily.
  5. Test the task manually once, then check the next morning that a fresh dated folder appeared in both destinations.

A cloud-synced folder (any reputable provider) gives you the off-site copy without a manual upload. The routine below shows the full loop.

Common mistake: Scheduling the backup while Tally is still open on a shared machine. The copy runs, the folder looks complete, and nobody notices until a restore fails months later. Close the company first, or script the job to run only when Tally is not running.

Backups that survive corruption, not just hardware failure

Most owners back up against a dead hard disk. The harder risks are file corruption, ransomware that encrypts every connected drive, and quiet human error that is only spotted weeks on. The 3-2-1 rule answers all three: keep three copies of your data, on two different media, with at least one copy off-site. In practice that is the live data, a dated backup on an external or network drive, and a cloud copy. The table compares the common approaches.

MethodProtects againstWeaknessRestore-tested?
Copy numbered folder on same PCAccidental deletion inside TallyDisk failure, ransomware, theft wipe both copiesRarely
Tally built-in backup to same diskUser error, quick rollbackSingle disk, single dated copy often overwrittenSometimes
Scripted daily copy to second drive plus cloud (3-2-1)Disk failure, corruption, ransomware, theft, fireNeeds setup and a monthly restore testYes, if you test

For sensitive books, combine the routine with Tally Vault so the data is encrypted at rest, and restrict who can reach the folder over the network via remote Tally access controls.

How to restore a Tally backup

Restoring is where good routines are proven or exposed. From the TallyPrime Gateway, choose Data, then Restore, set the source path to the backup folder holding TBK900.001 and TBK900.CFG, set the destination to a fresh empty folder rather than your live data folder, and select the company. Restoring over the working folder can overwrite current vouchers, so always restore to a new location, open the restored company, and check the Trial Balance and closing balances before you rely on it.

CA Tip: Do a real restore test once a month, not just a backup. A backup you have never restored is only a hope. Restoring to a spare folder and matching the general ledger totals against last month's figures takes ten minutes and is the only thing that proves your routine works.

How to recover damaged Tally data

If a company will not open or throws errors, TallyPrime's Rewrite can rebuild the data files. Back up the damaged folder first, then trigger Rewrite from the company selection screen and confirm. Rewrite repairs index and structural damage but it does not recover vouchers that were never written or were already lost, which is exactly why a dated backup is the real protection. To move a company to another computer, copy the numbered folder to the same data path on the second machine while Tally is closed on both; copying a folder is not a substitute for a proper backup, because a partially written folder gives no error until you open it. If you are also weighing a version move, our comparison of Tally Prime versus Tally ERP 9 explains what changed, and the Tally XML export is worth keeping as a portable secondary copy of masters and vouchers.

Worked example: what data loss actually costs

Owners under-invest in backups because the loss feels abstract. Put numbers on it. Suppose a disk fails and the last usable copy is six months old. The figures below are indicative and Exl GST.

ItemBasisAmount (INR)
Vouchers to re-enter6 months, ~300 per month = 1,800 vouchers1,800
Re-entry time1,800 vouchers at 15 per hour = 120 hours120 hrs
Bookkeeper cost120 hours at 450 per hour (indicative)54,000
GSTR reconciliation redone6 months at 2,500 per month (indicative)15,000
Estimated cost of the gapRe-entry plus reconciliation69,000

Against that, a scripted daily backup to a second drive and a cloud folder costs a few thousand rupees a year of storage and an hour to set up. The arithmetic makes the case on its own. The lost time also delays return filing, which is why keeping clean books feeds directly into work like filing GST returns using Tally Prime and generating e-way bills and e-invoices in Tally.

How long must you keep Tally records?

Backups are also a statutory duty, not only an IT choice. Under GST law, Section 36 of the CGST Act requires a registered person to keep books and records until the expiry of 72 months (six years) from the due date of the annual return for that year, as set out by the CBIC. Under the Companies Act 2013, Section 128(5) requires a company's books to be preserved for not less than eight financial years, per the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Income Tax record-keeping rules add their own retention period, detailed by the Income Tax Department. Your dated Tally backups are how you actually satisfy these periods years after the events. Once the data is safe and current, routine period-end tasks such as running a depreciation calculation and reconciling the bank reconciliation stay reliable because the underlying records can always be reproduced.

Key terms

  • Tally Vault: a password feature that encrypts a company's data at rest so the folder cannot be opened without the vault key.
  • Tally XML Export: a portable export of masters and vouchers, useful as a secondary, software-neutral copy.
  • Remote Tally Access: controlled access to a Tally company over a network, which needs its own security and folder permissions.
  • Trial Balance: the report you check after a restore to confirm the data is complete and balances match.
  • General Ledger: the full record of every account whose totals you verify against a prior period after restoring.

Key takeaways

  • One copy on one machine is not a backup; keep three copies, on two media, with one off-site.
  • Close the company before any copy or backup, or the copy can fail silently on restore.
  • Automate with Windows Task Scheduler and dated folders, since TallyPrime has no built-in scheduler.
  • Always restore to a fresh empty folder and verify the Trial Balance before trusting a backup.
  • Test a real restore monthly, and keep backups for the years that GST, Companies Act and Income Tax rules require.

If keeping this routine running reliably is more than your team wants to manage in-house, that is a service question rather than a how-to one, and our Tally Prime accounting services team can own the backup, reconciliation and month-end close for you.

Decision guide
key_points:
• A safe Tally data backup means a dated, tested copy that lives on a second drive and in the cloud, not just the numbered company folder sitting on one machine.
  • Close the company before you copy or back up: files open inside TallyPrime can copy incompletely and fail silently on restore.
  • Follow the 3-2-1 rule (three copies, two media, one off-site) so a backup survives file corruption, ransomware and theft, not only a dead hard disk.
  • Always restore to a fresh empty folder and verify the Trial Balance before you trust a backup; never restore over the live data folder.
  • GST, Companies Act and Income Tax rules require books to be preserved for years, so a backup is a compliance obligation, not just an IT nicety.

title: Does Xero Work for Indian Businesses? A GST and Compliance Check
content:
Xero works in India as a general ledger and invoicing platform, but the honest answer to xero in india gst is that GST is not built in the way it is in an India-first product. Xero has no localised Indian edition. You can record GST using custom tax rates and read it back on your reports, yet the statutory layer that decides compliance (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, e-invoicing and e-way bills) sits outside the software and has to be bridged every month. This guide sets out exactly what Xero handles natively, what India needs bolted on, and the one number that usually settles the decision.

Is Xero available in India, and which country owns Xero?

Xero is a cloud accounting product from Xero Limited, a company headquartered in Wellington, New Zealand, and listed in Australia. It is sold globally and Indian businesses can subscribe without difficulty, usually on the Global edition. What India does not get is a country-specific version with pre-built GST returns, an e-invoicing connection or a TDS module, the way Australian users get BAS or UK users get Making Tax Digital. So Xero is available in India, but it arrives as a strong general ledger and bank-reconciliation engine rather than a ready-made Indian compliance suite. If native Indian filing is your first priority, the usual comparison is Xero versus Zoho Books, and for a serviced setup you would look at Zoho Books Accounting or Tally Prime Accounting Services.

Does Xero support GST, and what has to be bridged?

Xero supports the mechanics of GST but not the filing. You can create custom tax rates, apply them on invoices and bills, and see GST collected and GST paid on your reports. What Xero cannot do for the Indian market, out of the box, is the following.

  • GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B: there is no India return that maps your ledgers to the GST portal, so returns are prepared in a separate GST tool from exported data.
  • E-invoicing (IRN and QR code): Xero has no connection to the Invoice Registration Portal. Businesses above the Rs 5 crore turnover threshold have to push invoice data to a GST Suvidha Provider and bring the IRN and QR code back onto the printed invoice.
  • E-way bills: generated outside Xero on the government portal or through the same bridge.
  • TDS: there is no module for sections 194C, 194J or 194I, so deductions are tracked through liability ledgers plus a spreadsheet, and Form 26Q is filed separately.

The workflow below is what a bridged setup looks like in practice.

CA Tip: Decide the bridge before you migrate, not after. The cleanest arrangement is Xero for books and one GST tool that reads Xero's exported sales register, so the IRN comes back on the invoice before it reaches the customer, never afterwards.

How to enable GST in Xero

Enabling GST in Xero is a matter of building the tax rates yourself, because there is no India default set. The steps are short but the accuracy of everything downstream depends on getting them right.

  1. Open Settings, then Advanced, then Tax rates.
  2. Create separate rates for the components you actually use: CGST and SGST as a paired rate for intra-state supply, IGST as a single rate for inter-state supply, and a 0% rate for zero-rated exports under an LUT.
  3. Build one paired rate per GST slab you sell at (typically 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%), naming them clearly so the person raising invoices cannot pick the wrong one.
  4. Map each rate to the correct ledger accounts in your chart of accounts so GST output and input land in the right control accounts.
  5. Set the default tax treatment on each contact (registered, unregistered, SEZ or overseas) so invoices default sensibly.
Common mistake: Creating a single lumped 18% rate instead of a CGST 9% plus SGST 9% pair. The invoice total looks correct, but the GST breakup the customer and the portal expect is wrong, and your GSTR-1 workings will not reconcile line by line.

How to show GST on a Xero invoice and handle e-invoicing

Once your rates exist, GST shows on the invoice by selecting the correct paired or single rate on each line. Xero then displays the tax breakup and the invoice total. The gap is the IRN. For a business over the e-invoicing threshold, a printed invoice must carry a valid Invoice Reference Number and QR code, and Xero has no way to obtain these on its own. The invoice data has to go out to a GST Suvidha Provider or e-invoicing tool, the IRN and QR code come back, and only then is the invoice valid to send. That handoff is the single most fragile point in a Xero-in-India setup and has to be controlled by a defined process. The threshold and applicability are set by the CBIC and are worth confirming against the source at cbic-gst.gov.in.

How to get a GST report from Xero and reconcile GST

Xero will give you a GST summary from the tax rates you built, showing output and input tax for the period. You use that as working data, not as a filed return. Reconciling GST in Xero means three things: agreeing Xero's output tax to the sales register you file in GSTR-1, agreeing input tax to your GSTR-2B so you only claim credit that actually appears there, and agreeing the net to what you pay in GSTR-3B, a discipline that runs alongside your normal bank reconciliation. The GST portal itself is the reference for what has been filed and what 2B shows, at gst.gov.in. Xero's bank feeds and reconciliation keep the cash side clean, and its bank rules speed up coding, but the GST-to-portal reconciliation is a manual monthly discipline. The monthly rhythm looks like this.

Why is Xero not calculating GST correctly?

When Xero appears to get GST wrong, the cause is almost always a setup issue rather than a software fault, because Xero only calculates what you told it to.

  • Wrong rate on the contact: an inter-state customer defaulted to CGST plus SGST instead of IGST, or an export contact not set to zero-rated.
  • Rounding differences: Xero rounds tax per line, and the portal or your GST tool may round on the invoice total, creating paise-level gaps that add up.
  • Rate mapped to the wrong ledger: the number is right on the invoice but sits in the wrong control account, so your reconciliation breaks.
  • Reverse charge not modelled: Xero has no native reverse-charge handling, so GTA and other RCM liabilities have to be posted by a manual journal entry.

None of these are reasons to abandon Xero. They are reasons to lock the setup down and review it before each filing.

Worked example: GST on a domestic invoice versus an export under LUT

This is the case most Xero-in-India users care about, because they typically bill both an Indian customer and an overseas client. Assume a services firm raises two invoices, each with a taxable value of Rs 1,00,000 (indicative, Exl GST). The domestic supply is inter-state at the standard 18% slab; the export is zero-rated under a Letter of Undertaking. The arithmetic is what your Xero tax rates must reproduce.

ItemDomestic inter-state supplyExport under LUT
Taxable valueRs 1,00,000Rs 1,00,000
GST treatmentIGST at 18%Zero-rated (0%)
IGST amountRs 18,000Rs 0
Invoice totalRs 1,18,000Rs 1,00,000
Reported in GSTR-1B2B, with GSTINTable 6A, export invoice

Both invoices are correct in Xero if the rates are built properly, but only the export needs the LUT reference and, on collection in foreign currency, an exchange gain or loss posting. That is where Xero's multi-currency bank feed earns its place, and why foreign currency receivables are cleaner to manage here than in most India-native tools.

Xero versus the India-native options at a glance

The realistic comparison for an Indian buyer is Xero against Zoho Books and TallyPrime. QuickBooks does not belong on this list: Intuit withdrew from India and customer access ended on 30 April 2023, so it is a migration source, not a choice.

CapabilityXero (Global)Zoho BooksTallyPrime
Native GSTR-1 and GSTR-3BNo, bridge requiredYesYes
E-invoicing (IRN)Via GSP onlyNativeNative
TDS moduleNoYesYes
Multi-currency and overseas billingStrongGoodLimited
Bank feeds and app marketplaceStrongGoodBasic
Best fitExporters wanting clean reportingDomestic SMEs wanting native GSTTrading and inventory-led firms
CA Tip: If more than half your revenue is billed to overseas clients and you value the automation and repeating-invoice workflows Xero is known for, the bridge cost is usually worth it. If your revenue is almost entirely domestic GST invoicing, an India-native tool removes the bridge entirely.

Is Xero free, and what does it cost to run in India?

Xero is not free; it is a paid monthly subscription, and in India the true cost is Xero plus the GST bridge tool plus the bookkeeping time to run the monthly reconciliation and TDS spreadsheet. Treat those three together when you compare it with a single native product. Depreciation and fixed assets are another area to plan, because Xero's fixed-asset register follows its own conventions and has to be reconciled to Schedule II of the Companies Act; our Depreciation Calculator helps square Xero's figures with the Indian schedule. For the commercial, serviced version of any of this, our Xero Accounting Services team runs the bridge for clients, and firms weighing an open-source route sometimes also look at Odoo Accounting Services.

Key terms

  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: the monthly check that you only claim input credit that actually appears in your auto-drafted 2B statement.
  • Xero Bank Rules: conditions that auto-code recurring bank transactions during reconciliation.
  • Multi-Currency Bank Feed: a bank feed that handles foreign-currency accounts and posts exchange gain or loss automatically.
  • Foreign Currency Receivables: invoices billed in a foreign currency and revalued to INR on collection.

Key takeaways

  • Xero is available in India but is not India-localised: GST, e-invoicing and TDS are not native.
  • You can record GST via custom rates, but GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, IRN and e-way bills must be bridged through a separate tool or GSP.
  • The Rs 5 crore e-invoicing threshold is the number that usually decides how tightly you must control the bridge.
  • Xero fits exporters and overseas-billing firms; domestic-only businesses are often simpler on Zoho Books or TallyPrime.
  • QuickBooks is not an option in India after 30 April 2023.

Decision guide
key_points:
• Xero is available in India, but it has no localised Indian edition, so GST, e-invoicing and TDS are not built in the way TallyPrime or Zoho Books provide them.
  • You can record GST in Xero using custom tax rates, yet GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, e-invoicing (IRN) and e-way bills must be bridged through a separate GST tool or GST Suvidha Provider.
  • Xero suits Indian companies that bill overseas clients in foreign currency and want clean management reporting, provided a compliance bridge is set up and run every month.
  • QuickBooks is not an alternative in India: Intuit withdrew and customer access ended on 30 April 2023.
  • The deciding number is your turnover: above the Rs 5 crore e-invoicing threshold, the bridge has to be tightly controlled or invoices go out without a valid IRN.

faq_items.answer: Xero is chosen for its bank feeds, clean multi-user interface, large app marketplace and strong multi-currency handling, which suits businesses billing overseas clients. Indian users normally pair it with a separate GST tool, because the compliance layer that TallyPrime or Zoho Books provides natively is not built into Xero for the Indian market.

faq_items.answer: Not natively. Xero has no built-in connection to the Invoice Registration Portal, so a business above the Rs 5 crore e-invoicing threshold has to push invoice data to a GST Suvidha Provider or e-invoicing tool and bring the IRN and QR code back onto the printed invoice. Form 26Q and 24Q are then prepared outside the system, which is where mismatches between the books and Form 26AS usually begin.

faq_items.answer: Zoho Books and TallyPrime are the two standard choices, both handling GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, e-invoicing and e-way bills natively, with Busy and Marg common in trading and distribution. faq_items.answer: It works well on the invoicing side, including multi-currency billing and automatic exchange gain or loss postings, but export documentation still sits outside it: the letter of undertaking, FIRC tracking, Softex where applicable and GST refund statements. Many IT services exporters run Xero for management reporting and keep a parallel file for Indian compliance.

title: Xero vs Zoho Books: A Comparison for Indian Businesses
content:
The short answer to xero vs zoho for an Indian business is that Zoho Books is built around Indian GST while Xero is a foreign-designed platform that reaches India compliance through add-ons. Zoho Books files GST, generates e-invoices and bills you in rupees out of the box; Xero handles the accounting well but leans on a GST Suvidha Provider or manual uploads for Indian statutory work. Which one is better depends less on the software and more on whether your revenue, banking and reporting sit inside India or straddle several countries. This guide compares the two on the points that actually decide the choice.

Xero vs Zoho Books at a glance

Both are cloud accounting tools that run proper double-entry bookkeeping behind a friendly interface, so the difference is not the bookkeeping engine but how each treats Indian tax, banking and cost. The table below summarises where they diverge for a business operating in India.

Point of comparisonZoho BooksXero
India e-invoicing (IRN, QR, e-way bill)Built in, generated inside the softwareNot built in; needs a GSP integration or manual JSON
GST returns (GSTR-1, GSTR-3B data)Native, India tax rates preloadedCustom tax rates; reporting largely outside the system
Free planYes, turnover below Rs 25 lakhNo free tier
Billing currencyIndian rupeesForeign currency (USD or GBP), FX charge on card
Multiple GSTINsEach GSTIN is a separate organisationNo GSTIN concept; tracked as custom tax rates
Indian bank feedsDirect feeds with several Indian banksMostly file import for Indian accounts
Audit trail reportIndia-specific report the auditor can testHistory and notes must be exported and explained

Which is better, Zoho or Xero, for Indian GST?

On GST the gap is wide. Zoho Books carries Indian tax rates, treats each GSTIN as its own organisation and connects directly to the invoice registration portal to produce the invoice reference number, signed QR code and e-way bill. Once your aggregate turnover crosses the Rs 5 crore e-invoicing threshold, that native link matters every day. Xero has no built-in India e-invoicing, so it needs a connector through a GST Suvidha Provider or a manual JSON upload, and GST returns are largely assembled outside the software. You can confirm the current e-invoicing rules and thresholds on the CBIC GST portal and file through the GST portal. For a business that lives entirely on Indian GST, this alone often settles the decision. Our deeper look at whether Xero works for Indian businesses walks through the workarounds in detail.

CA Tip: If you are already above the e-invoicing threshold, price the GSP connector into any Xero comparison from day one. Teams often quote Xero's base subscription and forget that the India e-invoicing piece is a separate paid add-on.

Is Xero cheaper, and does either offer a free plan?

Zoho Books has a genuinely free plan for Indian businesses with annual turnover below Rs 25 lakh, covering one user plus an accountant with caps on invoices and workflows. Xero has no free tier and is sold only as a monthly subscription per organisation, priced in foreign currency, which adds a foreign exchange charge on the card each month. So at the small end Zoho Books is not merely cheaper, it can be free. On the common question of whether Xero is cheaper than QuickBooks, the point is moot in India: Intuit withdrew QuickBooks from the Indian market and access ended on 30 April 2023, so QuickBooks is no longer a live option here. That leaves the real contest as Zoho Books versus Xero, and on rupee cost Zoho Books usually wins for India-only operations.

Why do accountants prefer Xero, and where does it fall short?

Xero earns loyalty for reasons that have little to do with Indian tax. Its bank reconciliation flow is clean, its general ledger and reporting feel polished, and its ecosystem of third-party apps is large and mature. Practices that serve UK, Australian or New Zealand clients often standardise on it, and that habit carries over. Xero is also beginner friendly: the interface is uncluttered and the learning curve is gentle, so it is not difficult to use for someone new to cloud accounting.

The disadvantages of Xero appear when you point it at Indian compliance. There is no native e-invoicing, no GSTIN structure, limited direct bank feeds for Indian banks, and GST reporting that sits outside the core product. None of these are flaws in the software as accounting software; they simply reflect that Xero was not designed for India. If you want a cheaper alternative to Xero for the Indian context, Zoho Books is the obvious one, and Odoo is worth a look for businesses that also need manufacturing or inventory depth.

Common mistake: Choosing Xero because "accountants prefer it" without checking whether that preference came from a UK or Australian practice. Their reasons rarely include Indian GST, e-invoicing or the Companies Act audit trail, which are the parts that will cost you time here.

Is Xero the same as Tally?

No. Xero is a cloud-first, subscription platform accessed through a browser, while Tally Prime is a desktop-rooted product with strong Indian statutory features and a large installed base of accountants who know it. Xero and Tally sit at opposite ends: Xero is modern cloud with weak native India compliance, Tally is India-native with a more traditional interface. Zoho Books sits in between, cloud-first like Xero but built for India like Tally. Do big companies use Xero? Larger firms tend to move to full ERP systems as complexity grows, but plenty of mid-sized and global small businesses run on Xero happily; in India, size and multi-GSTIN structure usually push growing companies toward Zoho Books or an ERP.

Bank feeds and reconciliation compared

Day-to-day bank reconciliation is where you feel the difference weekly. Zoho Books offers direct automated bank feeds with several Indian banks, plus statement import in CSV, OFX and QIF formats, so most Indian current accounts refresh with little manual work. Xero's direct-feed network was built for the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, so for Indian accounts it depends largely on file import. Where no direct feed exists, both need a daily or weekly statement upload, and both let you write rules to auto-match repeating transactions. Xero's rule engine and its Hubdoc document capture are genuinely strong; our note on how bank feeds and reconciliation work in Xero and the guide to Xero automation rules and repeating invoices cover the mechanics.

The Companies Act audit trail: a quiet but real difference

Since 1 April 2023, Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules requires accounting software used by companies to keep an unalterable audit trail of every change, and the auditor must comment on it under Rule 11(g). Both Xero and Zoho Books keep an edit history, so both can satisfy the rule. The practical difference is evidence. Zoho Books produces an India-specific audit trail report the auditor can test directly, while Xero's history and notes have to be exported and explained before the auditor is comfortable signing. You can read the notification text on the MCA portal. For a company under statutory audit, the easier report saves real time at year end.

Worked example: three-year cost for a growing GST business

Cost comparisons often stop at the monthly price, which hides the India-specific extras. The worksheet below compares a mid-tier Zoho Books plan against a comparable Xero plan for a company above the e-invoicing threshold, so the Xero side must include a GST Suvidha Provider connector. All figures are indicative, Exl GST, and the foreign exchange rate is indicative; check live pricing before you rely on the numbers.

Cost lineZoho Books (Professional)Xero (Growing) + GSP
Subscription per monthRs 1,499USD 42 at Rs 87 = Rs 3,654
Subscription per yearRs 17,988Rs 43,848
India e-invoicing / GSP add-on per yearIncludedRs 12,000
Total per yearRs 17,988Rs 55,848
Total over three yearsRs 53,964Rs 167,544

On these indicative figures the three-year cost of the Xero route is roughly three times the Zoho Books route, driven by the higher subscription, the foreign exchange margin and the mandatory GSP add-on for e-invoicing. The gap narrows if you genuinely need Xero's foreign-currency handling or a shared platform with an overseas group, in which case the extra spend buys something real. Track any software licences you capitalise with a simple depreciation calculator so the accounting stays tidy.

CA Tip: When you compare quotes, normalise everything to an annual, all-in, rupee figure including the GSP connector and the FX margin. A per-user monthly headline in dollars almost always understates the true Xero cost for an Indian company.

How to choose between Xero and Zoho Books

The decision is usually clearer than the marketing suggests. Work through it in order:

  1. Check where your revenue sits. Mostly Indian rupees and Indian customers points to Zoho Books; substantial foreign-currency billing or an overseas group points to Xero.
  2. Check your GST profile. One or more GSTINs, e-invoicing and e-way bills all favour Zoho Books, which handles GSTIN mapping natively.
  3. Check your banking. If your banks offer Zoho direct feeds, weekly reconciliation gets much lighter.
  4. Check your reporting and consolidation needs, including multi-currency requirements and how tightly your GST data must line up for GSTR-2B input tax credit matching.
  5. Price the full three-year, rupee, all-in cost, not the monthly headline.

If most answers land on the India side, Zoho Books is the pragmatic pick; if foreign currency and overseas structure dominate, Xero is worth its premium. For hands-on setup and migration on either platform, the Xero accounting services and Zoho Books accounting pages explain how we implement each.

Key terms

  • Xero Bank Rules: conditions that auto-code repeating bank transactions during reconciliation.
  • Hubdoc Automation: Xero's document-capture tool that reads bills and receipts into the ledger.
  • Zoho GSTIN Mapping: how Zoho Books links each GST registration to a separate organisation.
  • Multi-Currency Bank Feed: a feed that imports transactions in more than one currency for foreign accounts.

Key takeaways

  • Zoho Books is India-native: e-invoicing, GSTIN handling and rupee billing are built in.
  • Xero is a strong general platform with no native India e-invoicing, no free tier and foreign-currency pricing.
  • Zoho Books has a free plan below Rs 25 lakh turnover; Xero starts as a paid subscription.
  • Both meet the audit trail rule, but Zoho Books gives an India-specific report auditors can test directly.
  • Choose on where your revenue, GST and banking sit, then compare the full three-year rupee cost.

Decision guide
key_points:
• Zoho Books is built for Indian GST: native e-invoicing (IRN, signed QR, e-way bill), GSTIN-as-organisation handling and rupee billing.
  • Xero has no built-in India e-invoicing and no free tier; it reaches India compliance through a GST Suvidha Provider or file uploads.
  • Zoho Books offers a free plan for turnover below Rs 25 lakh; Xero is subscription only, priced in foreign currency.
  • Both meet the Companies Act audit trail rule since 1 April 2023, but Zoho Books gives an India-specific audit trail report the auditor can test directly.
  • For most India-only businesses Zoho Books fits GST and cost better; Xero suits those with a real foreign-currency or overseas-group need.

faq_items.question: Which of Xero and Zoho Books supports Indian e-invoicing?
faq_items.answer: Zoho Books connects to the invoice registration portal and produces the invoice reference number, signed QR code and e-way bill from inside the software. faq_items.question: Does Xero or Zoho Books offer a free plan in India?
faq_items.answer: Zoho Books has a free plan for Indian businesses with annual turnover below Rs 25 lakh, covering one user plus an accountant with caps on invoices and workflows. Xero has no free tier and is sold only as a monthly subscription per organisation. Paid Zoho Books plans are billed in rupees, which also avoids foreign exchange charges on the card.

faq_items.question: Which software handles multiple GSTINs better?
faq_items.answer: Zoho Books treats each GSTIN as a separate organisation with its own subscription, while branches inside one state sit within a single organisation. Xero has no GSTIN concept, so each registration becomes a separate organisation and GST is tracked through custom tax rates and reported outside the system. Consolidation in both cases happens in a spreadsheet or in Zoho Analytics.

faq_items.question: Do Xero and Zoho Books both meet the Companies Act audit trail rule?
faq_items.answer: Both keep an unalterable history of changes, which is what Rule 3(1) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules has required since 1 April 2023. The practical difference is evidence: Zoho Books produces an India specific audit trail report the auditor can test directly, while Xero's history and notes have to be exported and explained. The auditor then comments under Rule 11(g).

faq_items.question: How do bank feeds for Indian banks compare between the two?
faq_items.answer: Zoho Books offers direct feeds with several Indian banks including ICICI, HDFC and Yes Bank, plus statement import in CSV, OFX and QIF formats. Xero depends largely on file import for Indian accounts, because its direct feed network was built for the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand. Where no direct feed exists, both need a daily or weekly statement upload.

title: How Bank Feeds and Reconciliation Work in Xero
content:
Bank reconciliation in Xero means matching every line on your bank statement to a transaction already recorded in the ledger, an invoice, a bill or a payment, and then confirming that match on the reconcile screen. Xero pulls in the statement lines (through a live feed abroad or a manual import in India), suggests what each one relates to, and turns green once the two sides agree. The software does most of the matching, but a human still confirms each line, which is exactly where accuracy is won or lost. This guide explains how feeds and reconciliation work in practice for Indian businesses, and where the common traps sit. If you would rather hand the monthly close to a team, our Xero Accounting Services cover the full cycle.

Does Xero do bank reconciliation, and how far does it automate it?

Yes, reconciliation is the core of Xero. Every bank account has a reconcile screen with two columns: the statement line on the left and Xero's suggested match on the right. When they agree, you click OK and the line is reconciled. Xero automates the matching, not the judgement. It will propose a match when a statement amount equals an unpaid invoice or bill, apply any bank rules you have written, and remember contacts you have coded before. What it cannot do is decide that a payment marked "NEFT CR" is actually a customer refund rather than a sale. That call is yours, so "automatic bank reconciliation" in Xero is better read as "assisted": the line is suggested, you confirm it. This is standard double-entry bookkeeping with a faster front end.

CA Tip: Reconcile little and often. A green "0 items to reconcile" banner on the dashboard is only trustworthy if you check it weekly; a month of unmatched lines is far harder to unpick than five days of them.

How Xero bank feeds work in India

Outside India, Xero connects directly to many banks and pulls transactions automatically, usually refreshing once a day overnight, with a few direct feeds updating several times a day. Indian banks rarely offer this, so most Indian users have no live feed at all and import statements instead. That is not a limitation on reconciliation itself, only on how the lines arrive. You export a statement from net banking and bring it into Xero under Accounting, Bank Accounts, Manage Account, Import a Statement. Xero accepts CSV, OFX, QIF and QBO files. For a plain CSV you map the columns to date, description, amount and reference.

The single biggest import mistake is the date format. Indian statements are almost always dd/mm/yyyy, and if Xero reads them as mm/dd/yyyy the whole file posts into the wrong period. Set the format before you upload, and check that the first and last dates look right afterwards. If you run several accounts, current, EEFC, credit card, Xero handles multiple bank accounts happily, each with its own reconcile screen and its own feed or import routine. For a wider view of whether the platform suits local compliance, see Does Xero Work for Indian Businesses? A GST and Compliance Check.

How to reconcile a bank account in Xero, step by step

Once the lines are in, the reconcile screen drives the work. The fastest way to reconcile is to let Xero's suggestions do the routine matching and to reserve your attention for the lines it cannot place.

  1. Open the bank account and click Reconcile; Xero lists each unmatched statement line.
  2. Where Xero shows a green Match with an existing invoice or bill, check the amount and contact, then click OK.
  3. For lines with no invoice (bank charges, fuel, a subscription), use the Create tab to code the contact, account and GST rate in place.
  4. Where a bank rule fires, review the suggested coding before confirming; the rule proposes, you approve.
  5. For money moved between your own accounts, use the Transfer tab and pick the other account.
  6. Work down until the screen reads zero items, then open the bank reconciliation report to confirm the ledger agrees with the statement.

Reconciling invoices specifically is the same motion: when a customer pays, the receipt appears as a statement line, Xero matches it to the open sales invoice, and confirming the line marks the invoice paid and updates the general ledger in one step. If you need this handled at volume across accounts, our bank and credit card reconciliation services and accounts reconciliation and audit teams do exactly this.

Bank rules: coding faster without hiding errors

Bank rules are Xero's real time saver and its quietest risk. You create them from Accounting, Bank Accounts, Bank Rules, set conditions on the payee, description or amount, and fix the contact, account code and tax rate to apply. A rule that codes any line containing "Airtel" to telephone expense at 18% GST removes a lot of repetitive keying. The threshold to understand is this: a rule only suggests an entry, it does not auto-reconcile it. Each statement line still has to be confirmed on the reconcile screen, which is your chance to catch a rule coding something it should not.

The danger is a rule written too broadly. A condition on "transfer" or a bare amount can swallow genuine one-off transactions and post them to a default account where nobody looks again. Keep conditions specific, prefer the contact or a distinctive part of the narration over round amounts, and review what a rule actually did for the first month before you trust it. The current GST rate you hard-code into a rule should match the CBIC rate notifications for that supply; a rule set once and forgotten will keep applying an old rate after a change.

Common mistake: Treating a bank rule as done work. The rule turns the line orange with a suggestion, not green. If you bulk-confirm without reading, a mis-scoped rule can post months of entries to the wrong ledger before anyone notices in the general ledger.

Handling bank transfers and multiple accounts

Money moving between your own accounts is the classic double-counting trap. If you reconcile the outgoing leg as a payment and the incoming leg as a receipt, you create two unrelated entries and inflate reported turnover. Use the Transfer tab on the reconcile screen of one account, pick the other account, and Xero creates a single transfer that clears both sides at once. Where the two legs fall in different months, for example a sweep initiated on the 31st that lands on the 1st, route them through a bank clearing account and match each side on its own date, so neither month shows a false gap. Credit card accounts behave the same way: the card is its own bank account in Xero, and the monthly payment from your current account is a transfer, not an expense.

Why is Xero not reconciling? Common causes

When a reconcile screen refuses to go green, the cause is almost always one of a handful of things rather than a software fault.

  • Duplicate imports: the same statement period brought in twice, so lines appear against no real balance. Delete the duplicate import statement lines, do not reconcile them.
  • Wrong opening balance: if the conversion balance or first import is off, every subsequent balance is off by the same amount. Fix the conversion balance, not the individual lines.
  • Date format: lines posted to the wrong month from a mm/dd/yyyy misread; re-import with the correct format.
  • Unpresented cheques and deposits in transit: genuine timing differences that resolve when the item clears; these are not errors, they simply sit until the bank catches up.
  • Bank charges and interest not yet recorded: small debits the bank applied that are not yet in the ledger; code them on the Create tab.

The bank reconciliation report, found under Accounting, Reports, is where you diagnose these. It sets the statement balance against the Xero balance and lists the reconciling items in between, which points you straight at the difference.

Unreconcile versus Remove and Redo

Both options undo a reconciliation, and choosing wrongly wastes time. Remove and Redo, on the bank account's transactions tab, unreconciles the statement line and sends it back to the reconcile screen while leaving the underlying invoice or bill fully intact. Use it when the line was matched to the wrong thing but the invoice itself is fine. Unreconcile is used where the entry is correct but simply attached to the wrong statement line, and you want to keep the entry and re-point it. Both actions are recorded in History and Notes, so the audit trail stays complete either way, which matters when a reviewer or auditor later asks why a line changed. Automations like these are covered further in Xero Automation: Rules, Repeating Invoices and Workflows.

Worked example: a month-end bank reconciliation

Suppose your current account statement closes on 31 July at a balance that does not match Xero, because of one uncleared cheque, one deposit still in transit, and bank charges Xero has not yet recorded. The worksheet below reconciles the two. All figures are illustrative.

LineDetailAmount (INR)
Balance as per bank statement (31 Jul)Closing balance shown by the bank4,85,000
Add: deposit in transitCustomer cheque banked, entered in Xero, not yet credited by bank60,000
Less: unpresented chequeVendor cheque issued and in Xero, not yet cleared(95,000)
Adjusted bank balanceWhat the bank will show once both clear4,50,000
Balance as per Xero cashbookLedger balance before month-end coding4,50,767
Less: bank charges not yet recordedFee INR 650 plus GST at 18% (INR 117)(767)
Adjusted Xero balanceAfter coding the charge on the Create tab4,50,000

Both adjusted balances now agree at INR 4,50,000, so the account reconciles. The deposit in transit and unpresented cheque need no entry; they are timing differences that clear on their own. The only ledger action is coding the INR 767 charge, after which the reconcile screen reads zero.

Key terms

  • Bank Reconciliation: matching the ledger cash balance to the bank statement and explaining any difference.
  • Xero Bank Rules: saved conditions that auto-suggest contact, account and tax coding for matching statement lines.
  • Automated Bank Feeds: a live connection that pulls statement lines into the software, common abroad, rare for Indian banks.
  • Bank Clearing Account: a holding account used to park one leg of a transfer that spans two months.
  • Outstanding Checks / Timing Differences: items recorded in the books but not yet cleared by the bank.

Xero, Zoho Books and other options

The reconcile mechanics described here are broadly similar across cloud ledgers, but the feed situation differs. Because Indian banks rarely feed Xero directly, some businesses prefer a platform with local bank integrations. A side-by-side sits in Xero vs Zoho Books: A Comparison for Indian Businesses, and if you are weighing tools we also run Zoho Books Accounting, Odoo Accounting Services and Tally Prime Accounting Services. Whichever you land on, the discipline is identical: import or feed the lines, match against real transactions, and confirm every one. Where a reconciliation surfaces a fixed asset purchase, our depreciation calculator helps schedule it once it is coded, and the banking mechanics themselves follow the account-statement norms the Reserve Bank of India sets for scheduled banks.

Key takeaways

  • Reconciliation in Xero is assisted, not automatic: Xero suggests the match, you confirm each line.
  • Indian users usually import CSV or OFX statements monthly; set dd/mm/yyyy before uploading.
  • Bank rules save time but only suggest coding, so keep conditions specific and review the first month.
  • Use the Transfer tab for own-account movements to avoid inflating turnover.
  • Remove and Redo unmatches a line without deleting the invoice; Unreconcile re-points a correct entry.

Decision guide
key_points:
• Xero reconciliation means matching each bank statement line to an invoice, bill or payment already in the ledger, then confirming it on the reconcile screen.
  • Most Indian banks have no live feed into Xero, so the usual routine is a monthly CSV or OFX import with the date format set to dd/mm/yyyy.
  • Bank rules speed up coding but only suggest an entry; every line still has to be confirmed, so a badly written rule can quietly post to the wrong account.
  • Use the Transfer tab for money moving between your own accounts, or turnover gets double counted.
  • Remove and Redo unmatches a statement line without deleting the invoice; Unreconcile re-points a correct entry to the right line.

title: Xero Automation: Rules, Repeating Invoices and Workflows
content:
To automate repeating invoices and rules in Xero, you build a repeating invoice template that runs on a set cycle, and you create bank rules that code recurring bank transactions automatically. Both live in the standard Xero interface, both can be switched between fully automatic and review-first, and neither needs a paid add-on. This guide explains the automations that are genuinely worth turning on, the one setting that quietly creates rework, and how each behaves for an Indian business. For the commercial side of setup and ongoing bookkeeping, see our Xero Accounting Services.

What can Xero automate?

Xero automates far more than invoices. The main levers are repeating sales invoices and purchase bills, bank feeds paired with bank rules that code recurring transactions, invoice reminders that email a customer after a chosen number of overdue days, recurring journals for entries such as prepayment releases, and depreciation runs on fixed assets that post each period once the register is set. Payment matching during reconciliation is also semi-automated: Xero suggests the contact, account and tax treatment based on past coding. What Xero does not do in the Indian version is payroll and local tax filing, which are country-specific features. If you are weighing platforms, our note on whether Xero works for Indian businesses covers the GST gaps in detail.

CA Tip: Turn on one automation at a time and watch it for a full cycle before adding the next. When several new automations post together, tracing which one miscoded a transaction takes far longer than the setup ever saved.

How to set up repeating invoices in Xero

A repeating invoice is a template that generates a fresh invoice on a schedule you define, so you never re-key a monthly retainer or subscription. The setup runs in a few steps.

  1. Go to Business, then Invoices, and select New Repeating Invoice.
  2. Set the repeat frequency (daily, weekly, monthly or yearly) and the interval, for example every 1 month.
  3. Choose a start date and, optionally, an end date. Leave the end date blank for an open-ended retainer.
  4. Enter the customer, line items, account codes and the GST tax rate exactly as you would on a one-off invoice.
  5. Pick the automation level: Save as Draft for review each cycle, Approve to raise it automatically, or Approve and Send to email it to the customer without any manual action.

The same template engine drives repeating bills under Business, then Bills to Pay, which is useful for fixed rent or a monthly software subscription.

What is a repeating invoice, and how do recurring transactions work?

A repeating invoice holds no amount owed by itself; it is a set of instructions. On each due date Xero copies the template into a real invoice, dates it, numbers it and applies your chosen automation level. Recurring bills, repeating journals and scheduled depreciation all work on the same principle: a stored template plus a clock. Yes, Xero has recurring transactions across sales, purchases and the general ledger, and each type keeps its own schedule independent of the others.

How Xero bank rules work, and in what order they run

Bank rules are the second big automation. A rule watches your bank feed and, when a transaction matches its conditions, proposes a contact, account code and tax rate during reconciliation. Xero does not cap how many rules you create, and rules run in the order they are listed, top to bottom, with the first match winning. Reorder them under Bank Accounts, then Bank Rules, so that specific rules sit above general ones. Each rule targets spend money, receive money or transfer on a chosen account, and can be set to apply automatically or to ask for confirmation. Because the tax rate a rule applies feeds your GST working, code it against the correct rate under the current CBIC GST schedule rather than a default.

Rules cut coding time sharply on predictable items such as bank charges, payment gateway fees and recurring subscriptions. For the full reconciliation workflow, our guide on how bank feeds and reconciliation work in Xero walks through the matching screen step by step.

Common mistake: Writing one broad rule such as "any payment to a bank" and setting it to apply automatically. A wide rule quietly miscodes a whole class of transactions, and because it runs without a prompt, nobody notices until the trial balance looks wrong. Keep conditions tight and review rule hits monthly.

Can bank rules replace manual reconciliation?

No. A bank rule suggests coding; it does not post on its own. Each suggestion still needs a human OK before it hits the ledger, unless the transaction exactly matches an existing invoice or bill, in which case Xero can match it directly. This is a deliberate control. Reconciliation remains a review step, and the rule simply removes the typing. Treat rules as a first draft of the coding, not as a signed-off entry.

How to set up automatic invoice reminders in Xero

Invoice reminders chase overdue customers for you. Under Business, then Invoices, then Invoice Reminders, switch reminders on and set the schedule, for example a polite email 7 days after the due date and a firmer one at 14 and 30 days. You can exclude invoices below a rupee threshold so small balances do not trigger emails, and you can turn reminders off for a specific customer you would rather call. Reminders reduce the manual chasing that inflates your receivables ageing, though they do not replace a real conversation on a large overdue account.

Repeating journals, depreciation and bulk sending

Two more automations are worth knowing. A repeating journal posts a standing general ledger entry on a schedule, which suits prepaid expense releases or a fixed monthly accrual; set it up under Accounting, then Manual Journals, and tick the repeat option. Fixed asset depreciation runs post automatically once each asset is registered with a method and rate, so the depreciation charge lands every period without re-entry. And yes, you can bulk send invoices: select several approved invoices in the list and use Email to send them together, which pairs well with a batch of repeating invoices raised the same morning.

How can I use Zapier with Xero?

For automations Xero does not offer natively, Zapier connects Xero to other apps. A typical flow creates a Xero invoice when a form is submitted, or posts a Slack alert when a bill is approved. Zapier is useful for cross-app triggers, but it adds a moving part outside your ledger, so log what each connection does and review it when you change any linked app. For most Indian small businesses the built-in repeating invoices and bank rules cover the bulk of the need before any third-party tool is required.

Worked example: a monthly retainer on a repeating invoice

Suppose you raise a fixed monthly retainer of Rs 25,000 (indicative, Exl GST) to a domestic client, taxable at 18% GST. A single repeating invoice set to Approve and Send handles the whole year. The schedule below shows the arithmetic per cycle and across the year.

LinePer invoice (Rs)12 cycles (Rs)
Retainer (taxable value)25,0003,00,000
CGST at 9%2,25027,000
SGST at 9%2,25027,000
Invoice total29,5003,54,000

The automation raises and emails twelve identical invoices worth Rs 3,54,000 in total without any re-keying. One caution: the repeating invoice does not generate a GST e-invoice IRN. If your turnover crosses the e-invoicing threshold, the IRN must still be produced through the GST portal or your integrated tool, so keep that step in the workflow.

Key terms

  • Xero Bank Rules: conditions that auto-suggest contact, account and tax code on matching bank transactions.
  • Automated Bank Feeds: the live import of bank transactions that rules then code.
  • Hubdoc Automation: Xero's tool that captures bills and receipts and pushes the data into the ledger.
  • Bank Reconciliation: matching ledger entries to the bank statement, the review step rules speed up.
  • Journal Entry: the debit-and-credit record a repeating journal posts on a schedule.

How to turn off a repeating invoice in Xero

To stop a repeating invoice, open Business, then Repeating, select the template and either set an end date in the past or delete the template entirely. Setting an end date keeps the history and stops future cycles; deleting removes the template but leaves invoices already raised untouched. The same applies to repeating bills and journals. Before you switch off an automation that codes tax, confirm the last cycle posted correctly so you do not leave a gap in the period.

CA Tip: Diarise a quarterly review of every repeating template and bank rule. Retainer amounts change, GST rates move and vendors close accounts, and a template that ran perfectly in April can quietly bill or code the wrong figure by October.

If you run more than one accounting platform or are comparing options, the same automation ideas apply differently across tools. Our comparisons of Xero versus Zoho Books, plus the service pages for Zoho Books Accounting, Odoo Accounting Services and Tally Prime Accounting Services, set out how each handles recurring transactions. For the depreciation runs mentioned above, our Depreciation Calculator helps you check the charge Xero will post under Schedule II.

Key takeaways

  • Repeating invoices, bills and journals all run on a stored template plus a schedule, and you choose draft, approve, or approve-and-send.
  • Bank rules code the feed but run top to bottom with first match winning, so order specific rules above general ones.
  • Automation removes typing, not judgement: most rule hits still need a human OK before they post.
  • Automated invoices do not create a GST e-invoice IRN, so keep the portal step in your workflow if e-invoicing applies.
  • Review every template and rule each quarter, because rates, retainers and vendors change.

Decision guide
key_points:
• Xero automates repeating invoices and bills, bank feed coding through rules, invoice reminders, recurring journals and fixed asset depreciation runs.
  • Repeating invoices can run daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, and can be set to approve and email automatically or to sit as a draft for review.
  • Bank rules suggest a contact, account code and tax rate; they run top to bottom, first match wins, and each hit still needs a human OK unless it matches an existing invoice.
  • Automation saves coding time on repetitive items but does not replace GST e-invoicing on the government portal, so keep the IRN step separate.
  • Review rule hits monthly, because one broad rule can miscode a whole class of transactions quietly.

title: How to Set Up GST in Zoho Books (Step by Step)
content:
Setting up GST in Zoho Books means telling the software who you are for tax purposes so that every invoice, bill and return carries the right numbers. You do this from Settings, then Taxes, where you enter your organisation GSTIN, pick your registration type (regular, composition or others) and confirm your home state. Once that is saved, Zoho Books maps CGST and SGST to local sales and IGST to inter-state sales on its own, applies the correct rate from the HSN or SAC code, and keeps the data ready for GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B. This guide walks through the full setup in plain steps, with a worked tax calculation at the end.

Does Zoho Books support GST for Indian businesses?

Yes. The India edition of Zoho Books is built around GST and is a registered GST Suvidha Provider (GSP), which means it can connect to the GST portal and file returns directly. When you create your organisation on the India domain and set the country to India and the currency to INR, the GST features appear automatically. If you are weighing it against other platforms, our comparison of Zoho Books vs Tally for Indian SMEs sets out where each one fits, and the broader Zoho Books Accounting service page covers day-to-day bookkeeping beyond tax.

Before you touch a single tax setting, confirm your fiscal year is April to March under Settings, then Preferences, then General. GST return periods, opening balances and reports all key off this date, so it must be correct before you enter transactions.

How to enable GST in Zoho Books step by step

Enabling GST takes a few minutes once you have your GSTIN and registration certificate to hand. Work through these steps in order.

  1. Go to Settings, then Taxes, then GST Settings.
  2. Toggle Is your business registered for GST? to Yes.
  3. Enter your 15-digit GSTIN. Zoho validates the format and reads your state from the first two digits.
  4. Select your tax registration type: Regular for standard taxpayers, Composition for the composition scheme, or Special Economic Zone where relevant.
  5. Set the GST registered date so transactions before that date are treated as pre-registration.
  6. Choose whether you deal in reverse charge supplies and whether you have a digital services (OIDAR) obligation.
  7. Save. Zoho now shows GST fields on every invoice, bill, credit note and expense.
CA Tip: Enter the GST registered date exactly as printed on your registration certificate. If you backdate it, Zoho will let you raise tax invoices for a period when you were not yet registered, which creates a mismatch the moment you try to file.

How to add CGST and SGST in Zoho Books

You rarely need to create CGST and SGST manually. Zoho Books ships with the standard GST rate slabs already built in, and it splits a single rate into its two halves based on the place of supply. When the customer is in your own state, an 18% rate posts as 9% CGST plus 9% SGST; when the customer is in another state, the same 18% posts as a single IGST line. The software decides this from the customer billing state against your registered state, which is why keeping accurate customer addresses matters.

Adding a custom tax rate

If you need a rate that is not pre-loaded, go to Settings, then Taxes, then Tax Rates, and select New Tax. Enter a name such as GST18, set the rate, and mark it as a tax group if you want CGST and SGST shown as separate lines on the invoice. For a full walk-through of how the underlying ledgers behave, a basic grasp of double-entry bookkeeping helps, because each tax line hits a separate general ledger account.

Common mistake: Creating one flat 18% tax instead of using the CGST plus SGST tax group. A flat rate files the whole amount under a single head and the GSTR-1 summary will not tally with the return the portal expects. Always let Zoho split intra-state tax into its two components.

Setting up GSTIN mapping, HSN codes and place of supply

Three fields drive correct GST behaviour: the item HSN or SAC code, the customer GSTIN, and the place of supply on each transaction. Add the HSN code (for goods) or SAC code (for services) to every item under the item record so the rate applies automatically and the code flows into your returns. Record each customer's GSTIN on their contact so Zoho classifies them as registered (B2B) or unregistered (B2C). The place of supply defaults from the customer state but can be overridden on the invoice for cases such as ex-works delivery. Accurate GSTIN mapping is what lets the software decide CGST plus SGST versus IGST without you thinking about it.

Key terms

  • Zoho GSTIN Mapping: linking each contact's GSTIN so supplies are classified as B2B or B2C and taxed correctly.
  • GSTR-2B Input Tax Credit Matching: comparing your purchase records against the portal's auto-drafted GSTR-2B to claim eligible input credit.
  • Journal Entry: the underlying debit and credit record Zoho posts behind every taxed invoice.
  • General Ledger: the master account list where CGST, SGST, IGST and output tax balances accumulate.

How to enable e-invoicing in Zoho Books

e-Invoicing is mandatory for taxpayers whose aggregate turnover crosses Rs 5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18 onward, per the current threshold notified by the CBIC. To switch it on, go to Settings, then Taxes, then e-Invoicing. You then register Zoho Books as your GST Suvidha Provider on the government e-invoice portal, create an API username and password there, and enter those credentials back in Zoho. From that point, approved invoices generate an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and QR code automatically, and the details are reported to the GST portal in real time.

CA Tip: Keep the API password you set on the e-invoice portal recorded safely. It expires periodically and is separate from your normal portal login. When IRN generation suddenly fails, an expired API password is the most common cause, not a Zoho fault.

How to get GST reports and generate GSTR-1 in Zoho Books

Zoho Books keeps a dedicated GST section under Reports and a separate GST Filing workspace. To pull a return, go to GST Filing, select the return period, and Zoho compiles GSTR-1 (outward supplies) and GSTR-3B (summary) from the invoices already entered. You can review each section, spot invoices missing an HSN code or a customer GSTIN, and correct them before filing. Because Zoho is a registered GSP, you can push the return to the portal after OTP authentication, or export the JSON and upload it yourself. The mechanics of the full filing run are covered in our guide on how to file GST returns from Zoho Books, so we will not repeat them here.

For reconciliation, Zoho can pull back GSTR-2B from the portal so you can match your recorded purchases against what your suppliers have reported. This is the basis of your input tax credit claim and is worth doing every month rather than at year end.

How to record a GST payment in Zoho Books

After GSTR-3B computes your net liability, pay the challan on the portal, then record it in Zoho under GST Filing using Record Payment against the period. Enter the Challan Identification Number (CIN), the payment date and the bank account used. Zoho clears the GST payable ledgers so the balance nets to zero. Post any interest or late fee to a separate expense ledger rather than reducing the tax figure, otherwise your reconciliation with the portal will drift. If your bank feeds are connected, matching the payment is quicker; our note on automating bank reconciliation in Zoho Books explains that setup.

Worked example: CGST, SGST and IGST on one invoice

Consider a Maharashtra business raising an invoice for Rs 1,00,000 (Exl GST, indicative) at the 18% slab. The tax treatment depends purely on where the customer is. The table shows the same sale billed to a Maharashtra customer (intra-state) and to a Karnataka customer (inter-state).

LineIntra-state (customer in Maharashtra)Inter-state (customer in Karnataka)
Taxable valueRs 1,00,000Rs 1,00,000
CGST @ 9%Rs 9,000Nil
SGST @ 9%Rs 9,000Nil
IGST @ 18%NilRs 18,000
Invoice totalRs 1,18,000Rs 1,18,000

The customer pays the same Rs 1,18,000 either way, but the tax splits differently and lands in different heads on your GSTR-1. Zoho makes this call automatically the moment you select the customer, which is why an accurate billing state on every contact is not optional.

Common setup checks before you go live

Run a quick review once GST is enabled: confirm the GSTIN and registered date, check that every item carries an HSN or SAC code, verify each customer's GSTIN and state, and raise one test invoice each for an intra-state and an inter-state customer to confirm the tax splits as expected. If you run more than one platform, the same discipline applies to Xero, Odoo and Tally Prime setups, though the exact menus differ. Businesses evaluating cost can review our breakdown of Zoho Books pricing and plans. For a wider check on which reporting standards apply to your entity, the Ind AS Applicability Checker is a useful starting point.

Key takeaways

  • Enable GST from Settings, then Taxes, by entering your GSTIN and registration type before recording any transactions.
  • Let Zoho split intra-state tax into CGST plus SGST and use IGST for inter-state; do not create a single flat rate.
  • Add HSN or SAC codes to items and GSTINs to contacts so returns populate cleanly.
  • e-Invoicing is mandatory above Rs 5 crore turnover and needs Zoho registered as your GSP on the e-invoice portal.
  • Record GST payments against the period with the CIN, and keep interest and late fees in separate ledgers.

Setting up GST correctly at the start saves hours of correction at filing time. For hands-on help configuring or reviewing your Zoho Books tax setup, our Zoho Books Accounting team can take it from here.

Decision guide
key_points:
• GST in Zoho Books is switched on from Settings, then Taxes, by entering the organisation GSTIN and choosing the registration type.
  • Once the GSTIN is saved, Zoho maps CGST and SGST to intra-state sales and IGST to inter-state sales automatically, based on the place of supply.
  • Default tax rates (0%, 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%) come pre-loaded; you add HSN or SAC codes against each item so returns populate correctly.
  • e-Invoicing is enabled by registering Zoho as your GST Suvidha Provider on the e-invoice portal; it is mandatory above Rs 5 crore aggregate turnover.
  • Zoho Books is a registered GSP and can push GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B to the GST portal after OTP authentication.

faq_items.question: How to add an opening balance in Zoho Books?
